passages.section: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms
passages.text: "For the moms who shop our stores, back-to-school isn't just about checking items off their lists. It's about a fresh start, changing routines and getting children ready with products that match their personalities and budgets," said Duncan Mac Naughton, chief merchandising officer, Walmart U.S. "We're committed to setting our customers up for success this back-to-school season by sticking to our plan – offering everyday low prices and the broadest assortment of the right merchandise their families need." The "Walmart Class of 2012 Back-to-School Survey" also revealed that saving money and eating healthier topped moms' "new school year" resolutions, and uncovered moms' most important purchases for the season:

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

passages.text: Fiscal Years Ended January 31, STRATEGIC MERCHANDISE UNITS 2013 2012 2011 Grocery 55% 55% 53% Entertainment 11% 12% 12% Health and wellness 11% 11% 11% Hardlines 9% 9% 9% Apparel 7% 7% 8% Home 7% 6% 7% Total 100% 100% 100% Periodically, we make revisions to the categorization of the components comprising our strategic merchandise units. When revisions are made, we also adjust the previous period's presentation to maintain comparability.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Retail Sales Retail sales grew slightly over the reporting period and were up from a year ago. Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel. Sales growth in the Eleventh District remained stronger than the nation, on average, according to two large retailers. Retailers expect a seasonal pickup in demand in the fourth quarter, although sales will likely be down from last year. Automobile sales were mostly flat since the last report, but were up from year ago levels. Inventories were lighter than desired. Contacts said political uncertainty was hampering consumer confidence, and outlooks were cautious.

report.summary: Store 39's flagged departments sold below the ML forecast in the same way as most other Texas stores and many stores across Walmart that week. Walmart overall was nearly flat, and the Labor Day week is a possible calendar factor. No cause is verified, and the store-level markdown records cannot be tied to any department.

findings.title: Same drop across Texas stores
findings.text: In Texas, every other store sold below the ML forecast in Dept 3 Stationery, Dept 31 Accessories and Dept 24 Boyswear that week, and nearly every other store did so in Dept 33 Girlswear. This points to a drop shared across the region, not only at Store 39.

findings.title: Same drop at most stores nationally
findings.text: Across Walmart, 36 of 44 other stores sold below the ML forecast in Dept 3 Stationery, and 35 of 43 did so in Dept 31 Accessories. In Dept 99 Store Supplies, all 17 other stores were below the ML forecast. A shared pattern like this suggests a wider cause such as the category, the calendar or the economy.

findings.title: Walmart overall nearly flat that week
findings.text: All 45 stores together were at $48,296,614 against a $48,462,259 forecast (-0.3%), with 28 of 45 stores below the forecast. Store 39 as a whole was $1,609,812 against $1,722,405 (-6.5%), with 45 of 68 of its departments below the ML forecast.

findings.title: Labor Day week and fuel prices
findings.text: That week was the Labor Day holiday, and local fuel was $3.73 a gallon against $3.60 in the four weeks before. Temperature and unemployment were unchanged. These are possible calendar or cost factors, not verified causes.

findings.title: Earlier Dallas Fed report noted apparel strength
findings.text: The Aug 29, 2012 Beige Book for the Dallas Fed District said: "Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel." This describes the district before this week, and it points the other way from the apparel drops here.

departments.what_supports_it: This has the largest gap in dollars, $48,611 (-63.5%), and all 13 Texas stores were below the ML forecast in it that week. The ML team's notes say the last four weeks had a median of $83,643, so this week's $27,998 is a sharp change.

Accessories sold $2,459 against $6,935 (-64.5%), and all 13 Texas stores were below the ML forecast. The Dallas Fed report noted strength in accessories in August, which does not match this week's drop.
Boyswear was $7,104 against $11,775 (-39.7%), and all 10 other Texas stores were below the ML forecast, with 24 of 36 other stores flagged nationally.
Store Supplies was $20 against $153 (-86.8%), and every other store in Walmart and Texas was below the ML forecast. The dollar amount is small, so the percentage gap is large.
Menswear was $16,718 against $25,943 (-35.6%), and 10 of 11 other Texas stores were below the ML forecast, with 7 flagged.
Girlswear was $6,339 against $10,193 (-37.8%), and all 10 other Texas stores were below the ML forecast, with 9 flagged.

report.not_found: I looked for reports, outside factors or store records that explain drops in these departments for the Sep 7, 2012 week, and found none; the passages cover July, August and October 2012 and do not address this week in Texas.
next_steps: Check stock on hand and recent deliveries for Dept 3 Stationery and Dept 31 Accessories.
Check whether staffing or schedules changed during the Labor Day week.
Check pricing, displays and signage in Stationery, Accessories and Boyswear.
Check for local events, road works or new competitors near Store 39 that week.
Check sales records for Store Supplies and the other flagged units to confirm the figures were entered correctly.
Check the store's markdown records for that week; these are recorded for the whole store and cannot be tied to a department.
data_needed: Department-level sales and inventory for the weeks before and after Sep 7, 2012, to see whether the drop is new.
Department-level markdown records, since current markdown data is store-level only.
Store and department staffing schedules for the Labor Day week.
Records of competitor openings or promotions near Store 39 in early September 2012.

passages.text: Wages and Prices Price inflation remained quite limited for most final goods and services during the reporting period. Prices increased overall for some energy items including electricity, crude oil, and retail gasoline. Natural gas prices remained near historically low levels. Contacts noted high feed prices are passing through to grocery stores and restaurants. Contacts in the tech sector reported slightly lower prices of some technology-related products. For most products and services, vigorous competition among firms and cost-conscious purchasing behavior by consumers continued to keep price inflation in check.

Retail Trade and Services Retail sales rose further overall. Contacts reported sales were a bit stronger relative to the prior reporting period. Discount chains and online retailers continued to outperform traditional department stores. At grocery stores, consumer spending was soft as shoppers continued to shift their purchasing decisions in favor of cheaper products. Contacts reported a strong pace for auto sales, significantly above the pace from the same period last year. Demand for used vehicles also remained robust.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Our grocery business, which includes food and consumables, delivered a low single-digit positive comp. We continue to execute our strategic price investments, driving price separation versus our competition. Overall grocery inflation continued to moderate and was approximately 50 basis points, versus approximately 400 basis points last year. In food, our broad and localized assortment is resonating with the customer, as demonstrated by our continued strength in areas like dry grocery. In addition, strategic initiatives like our USDA steak program continue to produce encouraging results, with mid single-digit comp sales over the 39- week year to date period, exceeding the overall food comp by about 250 basis points. In the third quarter, our food business also delivered strong performance across the key seasonal events, including Labor Day, back-to- school, and Halloween.

During the 13-week period, both comp ticket and traffic rose for Walmart U.S., and both grocery and general merchandise had positive comp sales. "Our comp sales momentum continued through the second quarter, with July being one of our strongest months. All three geographic business units and all store formats had positive comp sales. Customers are responding to our continued focus on providing the right assortment at everyday low prices and are shopping the entire store," said Bill Simon, Walmart U.S. president and chief executive officer. "We have a powerful strategy and I'm confident in our ability to deliver sustained strong financial performance." For the 4-5-4 period from July 28 through October 26, Walmart U.S. expects comparable store sales to range from 1.0 percent to 3.0 percent.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Grocery, which includes food and consumables, delivered a low single-digit positive comp for the quarter. Our focus on winning key seasonal events paid off as we saw very strong food sales around the Fourth of July holiday. Another big success this quarter has been our USDA Choice steak program. The program has helped drive sales to the entire meat department, which outperformed the overall food business by approximately 300 basis points in the second quarter. The unmatched combination of quality and value has resonated with a large number of our customers, including many who had not previously shopped our meat department.

plan.why: The three largest dollar gaps (sporting goods, stationery, lawn and garden) are hardlines and home categories where the drop was broad across stores that week, so the search should test whether Walmart's quarter, regional conditions, or weather explain a pattern that the ML flag alone does not establish.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

"We were pleased that our constant currency sales and operating income were both up approximately 7 percent for the third quarter," said Doug McMillon, president and CEO of Walmart International. "We gained market share in almost all of our markets, indicating that our underlying business is performing well. We are working hard to improve execution where it's needed, and we're ready with great merchandise and price investments for the fourth quarter." U.S. comparable store sales review and guidance The company reported U.S. comparable store sales based on its 13-week and 39-week retail calendar periods ended Oct. 26, 2012 and Oct. 28, 2011, as follows:

Agriculture Drought conditions improved slightly due to scattered rainfall in July. Crops remained mostly in fair to good shape, with the exception of dryland cotton crop in the Texas High Plains region which suffered due to lack of moisture. Overall, crop conditions were much better than a year ago. Drought in the Midwest has caused grain prices to climb sharply, squeezing margins for ranchers by driving up feed costs for livestock.

These reclassifications did not impact the Company's consolidated operating income or net income. Additionally, certain prior period segment asset and expense allocations have been reclassified among segments to be comparable with the current period presentation. The Retail Industry We operate in the highly competitive retail industry in all of the countries we serve. We face strong sales competition from other discount, department, drug, dollar, variety and specialty stores, warehouse clubs and supermarkets. Many of these competitors are national, regional or international chains, as well as internet-based retailers and catalog businesses.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

report.summary: Store 6 was below the ML forecast in 60 of its 70 departments that week, and several flagged departments also fell at many other stores and across Texas. That points to a shared pattern, not only a local one. No holiday or report passage explains these specific departments, so the cause is not identified.

findings.title: Most of the store was below forecast
findings.text: Store 6 sold $1,372,403 against a forecast of $1,537,681 (-10.7%), and 60 of its 70 departments were below the ML forecast. Across all 45 stores, sales were $44,169,616 against $46,628,419 (-5.3%).

findings.title: Same departments fell at many stores
findings.text: Dept 3 Stationery was below the ML forecast at 43 of 44 other stores (median -24.2%). Dept 9 Sporting Goods was below at 38 of 44 other stores (median -13.3%). Dept 16 Lawn & Garden was below at 42 of 44 other stores (median -28.0%).

findings.title: Texas stores show the same drops
findings.text: In Texas, 13 of 13 other stores were below the ML forecast in Dept 3 Stationery, and 13 of 13 were below in Dept 16 Lawn & Garden. Dept 99 Store Supplies was below at all 5 other Texas stores.

findings.title: Outside factors show no clear link
findings.text: No holiday fell in this week. Local fuel was $3.72/gal against $3.63, temperature was 76°F against 85°F, and unemployment stayed at 5.7%. None of these is tied to these departments in the data.

findings.title: Company-wide focus on execution
findings.text: Walmart's Nov 15, 2012 earnings release said: "We are working hard to improve execution where it's needed." The release describes the whole company, not this store or these departments.

findings.title: ML team notes on model and season
findings.text: The ML team's notes say the model was too high at most stores for Dept 3 Stationery (97.7%) and Dept 16 Lawn & Garden (95.5%). They also cite a seasonal decline for Dept 16 Lawn & Garden and a recent decline for Dept 3 Stationery.

departments.what_supports_it: This store was at -24.0%, while 38 of 44 other stores were below forecast, and 11 of 13 Texas stores were below. The ML notes cite a recent decline (this week -26.3% against a last-4-week median).
This store was at -45.1%, the largest percentage gap among the flagged departments with broad evidence. 43 of 44 other stores and all 13 Texas stores were below forecast.
This store was at -31.7%. 42 of 44 other stores and all 13 Texas stores were below forecast, and the ML notes cite a seasonal decline.
This store recorded $0 against a $151 forecast. All 17 other stores and all 5 Texas stores were also below forecast, so this may be a data or recording question as well as a sales one.

report.not_found: I looked for a holiday, fuel, temperature or unemployment link, and for a report passage naming these departments or Texas stores, and found none.
next_steps: Check stock on hand and recent deliveries for Dept 3 Stationery, Dept 16 Lawn & Garden and Dept 9 Sporting Goods.
Check whether shelf pricing, displays or end-cap placement changed in these departments this week.
Check staffing levels and schedules for the week ending Sep 14, 2012.
Check for local competitor openings or promotions near Store 6.
Check the recorded Dept 99 Store Supplies sales of $0 for a data entry or register issue.
Note that the store-wide markdowns of $24,970 cannot be tied to any single department, so do not attribute the drops to them.

queries.name: stationery
queries.text: What did Walmart's FY2013 Q3 results and earnings call say about back-to-school demand and sales in stationery and office supplies?

queries.name: apparel
queries.text: What did Walmart report about apparel demand, including girls', accessories, and seasonal clothing, around August 2012, and how did weather affect those categories?

queries.name: regional
queries.text: What do the Atlanta or Dallas Fed Beige Books from August 2012 say about Gulf Coast retail spending, gasoline prices, and consumer demand?

plan.why: Dept 3, 31, and 33 carry the three largest dollar gaps, and the search should test whether category-level seasonality, Q3 company results, or Gulf Coast fuel and weather conditions could explain drops that were not seen across most other stores.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Home, including seasonal categories, had a low single-digit positive comp. Our continued focus on basics, supported by strong item merchandising and a refined assortment, drove strong performance in the quarter. Indoor living, led by cooking and dining, again performed well, as most departments posted an increased comp versus the first quarter. Back-to-school and back-to-college shopping is well under way. Our stores were ready to serve shoppers early in the season, and we're pleased with the results. Season to date, key back-to-school apparel categories are up 7.0 percent. Within home, we're seeing strong performance in college essentials like bedding and bath.

Natural Resources and Agriculture Contacts reported a renewed increase in production at Gulf Coast refineries because of recent closures along the East Coast. An increase in demand for crude oil and oil products, along with the Gulf Coast seeing particularly high demand for diesel fuels and other distillates, has helped to support refined product prices. Recent rains improved conditions in many parts of the District. Compared with the same time last year, prices paid to farmers for soybeans, corn, oranges, beef, hogs, and broilers were up while cotton was down. Although beef prices have increased over the last year, contacts reported that both the drought and high feed prices have resulted in lower prices paid to farmers on a month-over-month basis.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: So, let's get on to our results. Mike Duke will kick off the news for the third quarter. M
passages.text: Walmart U.S. posted a comp sales increase of 1.5 percent, and delivered approximately $2.3 billion in net sales growth. Back to school activities drove sales early in the quarter, and the mid-September launch of layaway was important in helping customers. Operating income outpaced net sales growth for the quarter and was a key driver of our overall company profit. Bill and his team are executing very innovative plans to drive traffic and to help America's families have a great holiday season. That's what our customers expect and we will deliver. We announced our extended Black Friday program, and customers are already working on their shopping lists.

passages.section: Walmart U.S. Neighborhood Markets and Other Small Formats
passages.text: • Apparel includes apparel for women, girls, men, boys and infants, shoes, jewelry and accessories; and • Home includes home furnishings, housewares and small appliances, bedding, home décor, outdoor living and horticulture.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: We had positive comps across all geographies and store formats. During the quarter, we focused on being the destination for back-to-school and Halloween shopping. Our merchants and operators developed a strong cross-functional plan, and I'm pleased with our execution and the sales growth achieved this year. As a reminder, a slightly larger portion of Halloween sales versus last year will fall into the fourth quarter comp period, given how the 4-5-4 calendar falls this year.

Petrochemicals producers reported steady demand. Demand for PVC, tied to residential construction, improved domestically, and exports continued to be a major source of sales. Exports of caustic soda remained strong as U.S. prices are very competitive due to lower electricity costs. Chlorine demand edged up, while demand for propylene weakened. Gulf Coast refiners said operating rates remained high at 90 percent. Robust export demand for gasoline and distillates kept inventories low, and refiners' margins remained healthy.

report.summary: Store 4 had 45 of 69 departments below the ML forecast and 14 flagged in the week ending Aug 24, 2012, but the store as a whole was $2,124,176 vs $2,186,742 forecast (-2.9%). Several flagged drops are shared by many stores, such as Outerwear & Swimwear, Cameras, Wireless Services and Stamps. Stationery and the apparel accessory departments are mostly specific to this store. No cause has been verified.

findings.title: Shared drops across many stores
findings.text: In Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear, 31 of 36 other stores were also below the ML forecast that week (median -34.2%). Dept 6 Cameras and Dept 58 Wireless Services show the same pattern across other stores, so these drops may reflect a wider trend.

findings.title: Stationery drop mostly this store's
findings.text: Dept 3 Stationery has the largest gap at $16,222 (-23.6%). Only 9 of 44 other stores were below the ML forecast in this department that week, with a median of +17.2%, and this store ranks number 6 from the bottom of 45. Nothing in the facts explains why this store differs.

findings.title: Apparel accessories and kids' drops mostly local
findings.text: In Dept 31 Accessories, Dept 33 Girlswear and Dept 24 Boyswear, this store is near the bottom of all stores. Most other stores were not below the ML forecast in these departments. The only other Gulf Coast store, Store 34, was also flagged in each of these departments, but that is a single store.

findings.title: Report context on apparel categories
findings.text: The Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call said "Season to date, key back-to-school apparel categories are up 7.0 percent." The 10-K defines the apparel category as follows: "Apparel includes apparel for women, girls, men, boys and infants, shoes, jewelry and accessories". This is national context only and does not describe this store's results.

findings.title: Outside factors and ML team notes
findings.text: The week had no holiday. Local fuel was $3.61/gal vs $3.42 and temperature was 76°F vs 82°F. The ML team's notes for Dept 36 list "model too high at most stores" and for Dept 48 "forecast may be too high", which are the ML team's own notes.

passages.source: Walmart news release, 2012-07-18: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms
passages.section: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms
passages.text: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms BENTONVILLE, Ark., July 18, 2012 /PRNewswire/ -- Walmart today announced the results of the "Walmart Class of 2012 Back-to-School Survey," which revealed that 76 percent of moms with children in kindergarten to 12th grade consider back-to-school a time for a fresh start over Jan. 1[1] – in fact, nine out of ten moms make back-to-school "resolutions" in preparation for the year ahead[2]. With 78 percent of moms planning to get organized[3] this new school year, Walmart today launched Classrooms by Walmart, an online compilation of thousands of classroom supply lists representing schools in all 50 states plus Washington, D.C., making it easier for moms to get their back-to-school supplies online and in Walmart stores.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Our apparel business posted a low single-digit comp increase, making this the third straight quarter of positive comps. The consistency of our apparel business and focus on basics, especially in kids, ladies, and men's, continues to drive growth, despite the impact of a warm October across much of the country. We have worked hard on improving item quality, focusing on the elements that our customers appreciate, and are optimistic that our current trend will continue into the holiday season.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

passages.source: Walmart news release, 2012-07-18: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms
passages.section: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms
passages.text: To view the multimedia assets associated with this release, please visit: http://www.multivu.com/mnr/57202-walmart-back-to-school-survey-online-supply-list-classrooms-moms (Photo: http://photos.prnewswire.com/prnh/20120718/MM40806) Classrooms by Walmart, the latest innovation to come from @WalmartLabs, enables moms to find their students' classroom supply lists and purchase the items on Walmart.com or at their local Walmart store. Walmart is the first major retailer to digitize thousands of school supply lists from across the country with additional lists to be added daily throughout the summer. Local school supply lists will also be available in Walmart stores.

passages.section: Walmart U.S. Neighborhood Markets and Other Small Formats
passages.text: • Apparel includes apparel for women, girls, men, boys and infants, shoes, jewelry and accessories; and • Home includes home furnishings, housewares and small appliances, bedding, home décor, outdoor living and horticulture.

Retail Sales Retail sales grew slightly over the reporting period and were up from a year ago. Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel. Sales growth in the Eleventh District remained stronger than the nation, on average, according to two large retailers. Retailers expect a seasonal pickup in demand in the fourth quarter, although sales will likely be down from last year. Automobile sales were mostly flat since the last report, but were up from year ago levels. Inventories were lighter than desired. Contacts said political uncertainty was hampering consumer confidence, and outlooks were cautious.

report.summary: Store 8 sold below the ML forecast in 16 flagged departments for the week ending Sep 7, 2012, with an ML estimate of $52,353 below forecast (not a verified loss). The same departments were also below forecast at most other Texas stores, while the store as a whole was $929,348 against a $965,761 forecast (-3.8%). No specific local cause was found in the data, and the reports reviewed do not name these departments for this week.

passages.text: "For the moms who shop our stores, back-to-school isn't just about checking items off their lists. It's about a fresh start, changing routines and getting children ready with products that match their personalities and budgets," said Duncan Mac Naughton, chief merchandising officer, Walmart U.S. "We're committed to setting our customers up for success this back-to-school season by sticking to our plan – offering everyday low prices and the broadest assortment of the right merchandise their families need." The "Walmart Class of 2012 Back-to-School Survey" also revealed that saving money and eating healthier topped moms' "new school year" resolutions, and uncovered moms' most important purchases for the season:

Retail Trade and Services Retail sales rose further overall. Contacts reported sales were a bit stronger relative to the prior reporting period. Discount chains and online retailers continued to outperform traditional department stores. At grocery stores, consumer spending was soft as shoppers continued to shift their purchasing decisions in favor of cheaper products. Contacts reported a strong pace for auto sales, significantly above the pace from the same period last year. Demand for used vehicles also remained robust.

Stationery (Dept 3) is the largest gap and looks mostly local, since most other stores did not fall in that department.

findings.title: Store and chain-wide sales both below forecast
findings.text: Across all 45 stores that week, sales were $47,131,887 vs $48,409,634 forecast (-2.6%), and 35 of 45 stores were below forecast. Store 10 was lower than that, at -8.7%, with 55 of its 68 departments below forecast.

findings.title: Apparel drops seen at many stores
findings.text: Outerwear & Swimwear (Dept 36) was below the ML forecast at 31 of 36 other stores, with a median of -32.9%. Accessories (Dept 31) was below at 26 of 42 other stores, with 15 also flagged by the ML team. This points to a category-wide pattern, not just a problem at this store.

findings.title: Stationery drop stands out at this store
findings.text: Stationery (Dept 3) was below forecast at only 14 of 44 other stores, with a median of +9.4%. Store 10's -39.0% is much larger than most stores, so the cause may be local, such as stock or display. findings.title: Grocery spending soft in Fed report
findings.text: The Fed's Oct 10, 2012 Beige Book, which is dated after this week, said "At grocery stores, consumer spending was soft as shoppers continued to shift their purchasing decisions in favor of cheaper products." This may fit the grocery departments flagged here, Infant Consumables (Dept 79) and Service Deli (Dept 80), but the report describes grocery stores as a whole, not this store.

findings.title: No holiday or local conditions changed
findings.text: No holiday fell in this week, and fuel, temperature and unemployment were almost unchanged from the four weeks before. The Fed's Aug 29, 2012 Beige Book said San Francisco retail sales were strengthening, with the rise "only 'a bit further'". This is general context and does not explain a drop at this store.

departments.what_supports_it: This is the largest gap, at $17,434 (-39.0%) below the ML forecast. Most other stores were not below forecast in this department, and the back-to-school release (Jul 18, 2012) mentions back-to-school supplies, which may be relevant but is not linked to this week.

This is the second-largest gap, at $11,559 (-27.1%) below the ML forecast. Most stores in the region were also below forecast, but with small median gaps (-4.9% across all stores), so the drop at this store is larger than most.
Furniture was below forecast at 25 of 36 other stores, with 9 also flagged, and at 2 of 2 region stores. The gap here is -23.4%, which is close to the median at other stores.
Jewelry was below forecast at 28 of 42 other stores, and at all 5 region stores, with 2 flagged in the region. The gap here is -23.9%, which fits a wider pattern.
This department shows one of the widest shared drops, with 31 of 36 other stores below forecast and a median of -32.9%. This store's -36.7% is close to that pattern.

report.not_found: I looked for a holiday, a big change in fuel, temperature or unemployment, and a report that names these departments, and found none that explains this week's gaps for Store 10 specifically.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Home, including seasonal categories, had a low single-digit positive comp. Our continued focus on basics, supported by strong item merchandising and a refined assortment, drove strong performance in the quarter. Indoor living, led by cooking and dining, again performed well, as most departments posted an increased comp versus the first quarter. Back-to-school and back-to-college shopping is well under way. Our stores were ready to serve shoppers early in the season, and we're pleased with the results. Season to date, key back-to-school apparel categories are up 7.0 percent. Within home, we're seeing strong performance in college essentials like bedding and bath.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Net sales, including fuel, were $14.2 billion, a 3.8 percent increase over last year's second quarter. Fuel prices in the second quarter were down 5.6 percent compared to last year, and gallons sold were up 3.9 percent, thus creating a drag on overall comp sales of 0.8 percent. Gross profit rate was up 23 basis points. Operating expenses as a percentage of net sales increased only 2 basis points, and operating income increased 10.1 percent to $535.8 million. Although fuel is an important traffic driver for the clubs, volatility in fuel prices can have a notable impact on our financial results. Therefore, the remainder of our discussion today is focused on our core business and excludes fuel for comparative purposes, unless otherwise noted.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Our apparel business posted a low single-digit comp increase, making this the third straight quarter of positive comps. The consistency of our apparel business and focus on basics, especially in kids, ladies, and men's, continues to drive growth, despite the impact of a warm October across much of the country. We have worked hard on improving item quality, focusing on the elements that our customers appreciate, and are optimistic that our current trend will continue into the holiday season.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Now, the remainder of our discussion today is focused on our core business which excludes fuel for comparative purposes, unless otherwise noted.Net sales were $12.2 billion, up 3.6 percent from last year. Our strongest divisional performance was in the West, with our strongest regional performance in the Great Plains, Mid South, and Mid Atlantic. Now I'd like to turn your attention to merchandising. There were three major themes during the third quarter: price investment, moderation of inflation, and new product introduction.

Retail Trade and Services Retail sales expanded a bit further overall. Respondents in general indicated that sales strengthened somewhat in July compared with softness in May and June. Performance was stronger for discount chains than traditional department stores, particularly for online sales. At grocery stores, extensive bargain hunting by shoppers caused sales revenues to weaken a bit. The pace of auto sales slowed somewhat compared with the prior reporting period, although it remained significantly above the pace from the same period last year. Used vehicles have been in short supply, raising their trade-in values and helping to spur sales of new vehicles.

report.summary: Store 10 sold below the ML forecast in 9 departments in the week ending Aug 10, 2012, and the store as a whole was close to forecast. Outerwear & Swimwear, Media and Horticulture fell at many stores, which points to a wider cause, but the largest gaps in Boyswear, Girlswear and Accessories were mostly seen only at this store or in this region. The national and district reports offer only general context for these departments.

findings.title: Outerwear and swimwear fell at most stores
findings.text: Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear was below the ML forecast at 34 of 36 other stores that week, so this drop is shared across the chain. The week was also warmer than usual (91°F vs 85°F), which is one possible factor, though it is not verified.

findings.title: Boyswear and Girlswear drops look local
findings.text: Dept 24 Boyswear and Dept 33 Girlswear were below the ML forecast at only 7 of 36 other stores each, and the median other store was above forecast in both. Store 10's drops are much larger than the chain pattern, so local causes such as stock, displays or staffing are worth checking first.

findings.title: Media and Horticulture softness across stores
findings.text: Dept 55 Media (expanded) was below the ML forecast at 32 of 36 other stores, and Dept 56 Horticulture at 25 of 38. Both were flagged at this store, but the wider pattern suggests a shared cause rather than one at this store alone.

findings.title: District report notes weaker grocery sales
findings.text: The San Francisco Fed report dated Aug 29, 2012, which is after this week, says: "At grocery stores, extensive bargain hunting by shoppers caused sales revenues to weaken a bit." This is district-wide and does not describe Store 10, but it is a possible context for Dept 80 Service Deli and Dept 83 Seafood.

findings.title: Chain-wide sales were not weak that week
findings.text: All 45 stores were $47,386,845 against a $47,102,033 forecast, which is +0.6%, and Store 10 as a whole was -1.0%. Walmart's Q2 call on Aug 16, 2012 said: "Season to date, key back-to-school apparel categories are up 7.0 percent."

departments.what_supports_it: Actual sales were $23,342 against a $39,665 ML forecast (-41.1%), but only 7 of 36 other stores were below forecast in this department. The ML team notes a seasonal decline signal.
Actual sales were $18,421 against a $28,182 ML forecast (-34.6%), and the median other store was +13.4%. The ML team notes both recent and seasonal decline signals.
Actual sales were $9,702 against a $17,913 ML forecast (-45.8%). Three of five West Coast stores were also flagged, which points to a shared regional pattern.
Actual sales were $2,846 against a $4,313 ML forecast (-34.0%), and 34 of 36 other stores were below forecast. The warmer week (91°F vs 85°F) is one possible factor.
Actual sales were $9,306 against a $12,359 ML forecast (-24.7%), and 32 of 36 other stores were below forecast with a median of -7.8%.
Actual sales were $337 against a $619 ML forecast (-45.5%). The SF Fed report describes weaker grocery sales in the district, though not for this store.

report.not_found: No report, outside factor or other store's pattern was found that explains the largest drops in Boyswear and Girlswear, which were not seen at most other stores that week.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

Natural Resources and Agriculture Contacts reported a renewed increase in production at Gulf Coast refineries because of recent closures along the East Coast. An increase in demand for crude oil and oil products, along with the Gulf Coast seeing particularly high demand for diesel fuels and other distillates, has helped to support refined product prices. Recent rains improved conditions in many parts of the District. Compared with the same time last year, prices paid to farmers for soybeans, corn, oranges, beef, hogs, and broilers were up while cotton was down. Although beef prices have increased over the last year, contacts reported that both the drought and high feed prices have resulted in lower prices paid to farmers on a month-over-month basis.

Indoor living, led by cooking and dining, again performed well, as most departments posted an increased comp versus the first quarter. Back-to-school and back-to-college shopping is well under way. Our stores were ready to serve shoppers early in the season, and we're pleased with the results. Season to date, key back-to-school apparel categories are up 7.0 percent. Within home, we're seeing strong performance in college essentials like bedding and bath.

passages.section: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms
passages.text: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms BENTONVILLE, Ark., July 18, 2012 /PRNewswire/ -- Walmart today announced the results of the "Walmart Class of 2012 Back-to-School Survey," which revealed that 76 percent of moms with children in kindergarten to 12th grade consider back-to-school a time for a fresh start over Jan. 1[1] – in fact, nine out of ten moms make back-to-school "resolutions" in preparation for the year ahead[2]. With 78 percent of moms planning to get organized[3] this new school year, Walmart today launched Classrooms by Walmart, an online compilation of thousands of classroom supply lists representing schools in all 50 states plus Washington, D.C., making it easier for moms to get their back-to-school supplies online and in Walmart stores.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Our apparel business posted a low single-digit comp increase, making this the third straight quarter of positive comps. The consistency of our apparel business and focus on basics, especially in kids, ladies, and men's, continues to drive growth, despite the impact of a warm October across much of the country. We have worked hard on improving item quality, focusing on the elements that our customers appreciate, and are optimistic that our current trend will continue into the holiday season.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

report.summary: Store 4's flagged departments sold below the ML forecast this week, and several of them also fell at many other stores. Walmart overall and Store 4 as a whole were also below forecast, while Stationery looks more local to this store. The store-side checks below can help narrow down the cause.

findings.title: Several departments fell at many stores
findings.text: Store Supplies was below the ML forecast at all 14 other stores that carry it this week. Womenswear and Girlswear fell at about two-thirds of other stores, and Home Management fell at 36 of 44. Broad drops like these point to a wider cause rather than something only at this store.

findings.title: Stationery drop looks mostly local
findings.text: Only 14 of 44 other stores were below the ML forecast in Stationery this week, and the median other store was above it. The largest shortfall is at this store (-39.5%), with a similar one at Store 34 (-44.8%). Local stock or display issues are worth checking first.

findings.title: Atlanta retail sales reported slower
findings.text: The Fed's Atlanta District report for Aug 29, 2012 says "In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales." This is a district-wide view, not a view of this store, and it is general context only.

findings.title: Walmart overall slightly below forecast
findings.text: All 45 stores this week came in at $47,131,887 against a $48,409,634 forecast (-2.6%), and 35 of 45 stores were below forecast. Store 4 was below forecast by -4.1% overall, so the store's gap is in line with a broader pattern.

findings.title: Weather and fuel prices changed this week
findings.text: Temperature was 76°F, compared with 82°F in the four weeks before. Local fuel was $3.65/gal, compared with $3.51. No holiday fell in this week, so these are possible contributing factors, not confirmed causes.

departments.what_supports_it: The drop is the largest in dollar terms ($18,136 below forecast), and ML notes say this week was -55.9% against the last 4 weeks' median. Most other stores were not below forecast in this department, so the cause may be local.

All 14 other stores were below forecast in this department, and this store was -98.4%. The drop is widely shared, which points to a wider cause, though the ML team's note on this department is a note, not a confirmed reason.
Store 34 was also flagged (-37.1%), and 19 of 36 other stores were below forecast, with 7 also flagged by the ML team. The overall median was only -1.2%, so most of the gap sits at a few stores.
This store was the lowest of 38 at -57.5%, though the all-store median was -0.0%. The gap is large here and not shared broadly.
This store was the lowest of 18 at -37.6%, while the other stores' median was -4.2%. The gap is large and mostly local.
26 of 42 other stores were below forecast, and Store 34 was flagged at -38.3%. Accessories is a shared apparel drop, but this store is still well below its peers.

findings.title: Store 4 has many departments below forecast
findings.text: 43 of Store 4's 70 departments were below the ML forecast that week, and 16 were flagged. The store as a whole was $2,124,098 vs $2,177,717 forecast (-2.5%). Some drops may be local, so the store's own stock and staffing records are worth checking.

findings.title: Walmart overall close to forecast that week
findings.text: All 45 stores together were $48,296,614 vs $48,462,259 forecast (-0.3%), and 28 of 45 stores were below forecast. Walmart U.S. comparable sales for FY2013 Q3 were +1.5%. The store-level gap is therefore not part of a large company-wide shortfall.

findings.title: Regional report notes slower retail sales
findings.text: A Federal Reserve Beige Book dated Aug 29, 2012 says "In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales." Store 4 may fall in the Atlanta or Dallas Fed district, and the report is from before the week in question. It is general context only.

departments.what_supports_it: 36 of 44 other stores were also below the ML forecast in this department that week, so the drop is shared. Store 4's gap was $7,407, the largest in the flagged list.
Store 4's gap was $3,175 (-26.2%), but the median across other stores was -1.4%, so the drop is mostly local to this store.
28 of 36 other stores were below forecast in this department, with a median of -38.6%, which supports a shared apparel pattern.
29 of 36 other stores were below forecast in this department, with a median of -31.2%, so the apparel drop is broad.
Store 4 was -68.6%, while the median across other stores was -6.4% and none of them were flagged, so this drop looks local to the store.
All 17 other stores were below forecast, with a median of -92.9%. The store's actual value was $0, which is worth checking in the sales records.

report.not_found: No report passage names these departments or explains a drop in them for the week of Sep 7, 2012, and no store-side data on stock, staffing, pricing or displays was provided.

report.summary: Several flagged departments were also below the ML forecast at many other Walmart stores in the same week, and in Texas. Infant consumables, store supplies and outerwear show the widest shared drops. The store as a whole was close to its own forecast, and no store-side or outside cause has been confirmed. Possible reasons are listed below for the analyst to check.

findings.title: Infant consumables fell at most stores
findings.text: Infant Consumables was below the ML forecast at 37 of 44 other stores that week, and at 10 of 13 other Texas stores. This store's drop was -21.6%, which is a shared pattern rather than one specific to this store. The ML team's notes say the model ran too high at most stores in this department.

findings.title: Store supplies and outerwear dropped widely
findings.text: Outerwear & Swimwear was below the ML forecast at 31 of 36 other stores, and Store Supplies at all 14 other stores. In Texas, 9 of 10 other stores were flagged for Outerwear & Swimwear. This store's drops in these departments are part of a broad pattern.

findings.title: Walmart was below forecast that week
findings.text: All 45 stores together sold $47,131,887 against a $48,409,634 forecast, which is -2.6%. 35 of 45 stores were below forecast, so this store's shortfall fits a wider pattern.

findings.title: Store-wide total was close to forecast
findings.text: Across all 70 of Store 2's departments, sales were $1,946,501 against a $1,950,556 forecast, which is -0.2%. Markdowns of $35,230 are recorded for the whole store and cannot be linked to any one department.

findings.title: Possible trade-down and outside factors
findings.text: Walmart's Aug 16, 2012 earnings call said "In categories with higher inflation, customers continued to trade down." This is a general statement about Walmart and does not cover this store. Local fuel was $3.64/gal against $3.53, and temperature was 83°F against 87°F. No holiday was recorded that week, and unemployment was unchanged at 6.6%.

departments.what_supports_it: Below the ML forecast at 37 of 44 other stores and 10 of 13 other Texas stores that week. This store's -21.6% is part of a wider pattern.
Below the ML forecast at 25 of 31 other stores, with 9 of those also flagged, and at 8 of 10 other Texas stores. The median across stores was -13.9%, so the drop is not limited to this store.

Below the ML forecast at 19 of 36 other stores, which is about half, with a median of -1.2%. Texas was below forecast at 7 of 10 other stores. The shared pattern is weaker here than in other departments.
Below the ML forecast at 23 of 36 other stores and at all 10 other Texas stores, with 7 of those Texas stores also flagged. This suggests a regional pattern.
Below the ML forecast at 31 of 36 other stores, with a median of -36.1%. All 10 other Texas stores were below forecast, and 9 were flagged. This store's -26.1% is part of a broad drop.
Below the ML forecast at all 14 other stores, with a median of -77.6%. This store's -84.6% is in line with the wider pattern, though the amount is only $20 against a $130 forecast.

report.not_found: I looked for store-specific evidence such as local stock problems, staffing changes, local competitors or local events, and found none in the data provided.
next_steps: Check stock on hand and recent deliveries for infant consumables, optical, outerwear and store supplies for the week ending Aug 31, 2012.
Check whether staffing or schedules changed in the departments flagged that week.
Check pricing, promotions and displays in the flagged departments, especially infant consumables and outerwear.
Check for local events or competitor openings near the store in late August 2012.
Check that the department sales figures for the week were entered correctly.

Delivery and out-of-stock records for the flagged departments.
Price change and promotion records for the flagged departments.
Competitor pricing or opening data for the Store 2 trade area.
Markdown amounts broken down by department, which are not in the data provided.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Comp sales in hardlines increased by low-single digits. We continue to see steady good performance in stationery, crafts, and sporting goods. Sporting goods had strong performance due to expanded hunting assortment, including guns and ammunition. The addition of key hardlines categories to layaway was attractive to customers, who also purchased items not on the layaway list.

passages.section: Walmart U.S. Neighborhood Markets and Other Small Formats
passages.text: • Apparel includes apparel for women, girls, men, boys and infants, shoes, jewelry and accessories; and • Home includes home furnishings, housewares and small appliances, bedding, home décor, outdoor living and horticulture.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Retail Sales Retail sales grew slightly over the reporting period and were up from a year ago. Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel. Sales growth in the Eleventh District remained stronger than the nation, on average, according to two large retailers. Retailers expect a seasonal pickup in demand in the fourth quarter, although sales will likely be down from last year. Automobile sales were mostly flat since the last report, but were up from year ago levels. Inventories were lighter than desired. Contacts said political uncertainty was hampering consumer confidence, and outlooks were cautious.

passages.source: Walmart news release, 2012-07-18: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms
passages.section: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms
passages.text: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms BENTONVILLE, Ark., July 18, 2012 /PRNewswire/ -- Walmart today announced the results of the "Walmart Class of 2012 Back-to-School Survey," which revealed that 76 percent of moms with children in kindergarten to 12th grade consider back-to-school a time for a fresh start over Jan. 1[1] – in fact, nine out of ten moms make back-to-school "resolutions" in preparation for the year ahead[2]. With 78 percent of moms planning to get organized[3] this new school year, Walmart today launched Classrooms by Walmart, an online compilation of thousands of classroom supply lists representing schools in all 50 states plus Washington, D.C., making it easier for moms to get their back-to-school supplies online and in Walmart stores.

report.summary: Store 11 sold $1,372,628 against a $1,429,962 ML forecast (-4.0%) for the week ending Aug 31, 2012. Walmart overall was -2.6% that week, and many stores in Texas and nationwide were also below the ML forecast in these departments. The drops look broad rather than limited to this store, but no report or outside factor directly explains them.

findings.title: Apparel and accessories drops are widespread
findings.text: Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear was below the ML forecast at 31 of 36 other stores that week. Dept 33 Girlswear and Dept 31 Accessories were also below the ML forecast at many other stores, including Texas stores.

findings.title: Hardlines drops seen at many stores
findings.text: Dept 11 Hardware was below the ML forecast at 32 of 44 other stores, and Dept 19 Fabrics & Crafts at 23 of 26. The Walmart earnings call said "Comp sales in hardlines increased by low-single digits," which does not match these drops, though it is Walmart-wide and not this store.

findings.title: Store-wide shortfall, larger than Walmart's
findings.text: 49 of Store 11's 69 departments were below the ML forecast that week, and the store was -4.0% overall against -2.6% for all 45 stores. The store's Dept 99 and Dept 36 drops are also larger than those at most other stores.

findings.title: ML team notes recent and seasonal declines
findings.text: The ML team's notes say Dept 58 Wireless Services was -48.6% against its recent four-week median and Dept 6 Cameras was -63.0% against the same season in earlier years. The notes also say Dept 31 Accessories shows both a recent and a seasonal decline.

findings.title: Dallas district reported lighter inventories
findings.text: The Dallas Fed Beige Book said "Inventories were lighter than desired" for the Eleventh District as a whole. This is district-wide and does not describe Store 11, but stock levels are a possible reason for the hardlines drop to check locally.

departments.what_supports_it: 32 of 44 other stores and 10 of 13 Texas stores were also below the ML forecast in this department. Store 11 was -22.8%, which is 4th from the bottom of 45 stores.
23 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast, and all 10 other Texas stores were below it, 7 of them flagged. Store 11 was -29.5%.
31 of 36 other stores and all 10 Texas stores were below the ML forecast in this department. Store 11 was -68.0%, but this is within a broad decline.
26 of 42 other stores were below the ML forecast, and the Dallas Fed reported "particular strength" in accessories, which does not match this drop. Store 11 was -41.4%.
23 of 26 other stores were below the ML forecast, and 7 of 8 Texas stores were. Store 11 was -34.7%.

report.not_found: No report, outside factor or other store's data was found that explains why Store 11's departments fell below the ML forecast; the holiday field was none and the other outside factors changed only slightly.
next_steps: Check stock on hand and recent deliveries for hardlines (Dept 11, 12, 19) and apparel (Dept 31, 33, 36) at Store 11.
Check whether staffing or shift coverage changed in these departments that week.
Check pricing, shelf displays and any end-cap changes for the flagged departments.
Check for local events or competitor promotions near Store 11 during the week ending Aug 31, 2012.
Confirm the week's sales entries for the flagged departments were recorded correctly.
data_needed: Store 11 weekly sales by department for the 8 weeks before Aug 31, 2012, to see whether the drops are new.
Store 11 inventory counts and delivery records for the flagged departments that week.
Store 11 staffing hours by department that week.
Local competitor price or promotion records for the Store 11 area.
Store-level markdown records by week, with department detail if available, to check whether any department-level timing matches.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Our apparel business posted a low single-digit comp increase, making this the third straight quarter of positive comps. The consistency of our apparel business and focus on basics, especially in kids, ladies, and men's, continues to drive growth, despite the impact of a warm October across much of the country. We have worked hard on improving item quality, focusing on the elements that our customers appreciate, and are optimistic that our current trend will continue into the holiday season.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Early availability of toys in our clubs has driven double-digit comp sales. Apparel was up a low single-digit comp and home achieved high single-digit comps. The continued introductions of new national brands and better assortment have driven sales growth. Recent innovations in mattresses are helping sales as well, and we continue to be a destination for this category. Health and wellness remains a growth category, with comps up mid- single digits. Sales of over-the-counter products are benefiting from the introduction of new diet trend products. E-commerce continues to help members access Sam's Club anywhere, anytime. During the third quarter, traffic was up and more members are utilizing our e-commerce solutions. Online sales of electronics and baby care are growing.

This was an 11.3 percent increase from the $0.97 per share reported for the third quarter last year.

Construction and Real Estate Single-family housing activity continued to increase at a good pace over the past six weeks. Contacts said new and existing home sales outpaced expectations, and new home construction activity increased. Inventories of both new and existing homes remained tight, leading to price gains. Apartment construction picked up since the last report, and outlooks for the multifamily sector remain quite optimistic. Leasing activity in the office and industrial real estate sectors remained steady at a good pace. While commercial construction remains at low levels, contacts expect activity to improve.

report.summary: Store 4 sold below the ML forecast in 16 flagged departments. Several Home departments were also below forecast at many other stores that week, which points to a wider pattern. Other departments such as Cameras, Boyswear and Hosiery were up at most other stores, so their drops appear specific to this store. No outside factor clearly explains the drops.

findings.title: Home departments fell at many stores
findings.text: Lawn & Garden, Furniture, Horticulture and Bedding were below the ML forecast at many other stores that week. The ML team's notes say the model was too high at most other stores in these departments.

findings.title: Some drops appear only at this store
findings.text: At other stores, Cameras, Boyswear and Hosiery were at or above the ML forecast that week (median +11.1%, +4.0% and +6.5%). At Store 4 they were below forecast by -33.2%, -21.5% and -36.5%, so these drops are not shared across stores.

findings.title: Store 4 was below forecast overall
findings.text: Store 4 sold $2,027,620 against a $2,096,925 forecast (-3.3%), with 54 of 71 departments below forecast. Walmart overall was -1.9% that week, so the store was somewhat weaker than the chain.

findings.title: Report describes Home and Apparel categories
findings.text: Walmart's FY2013 10-K defines Home as including "bedding, home décor, outdoor living and horticulture," and Apparel as including apparel for women, girls, men, boys and infants. These categories match the flagged Home and Apparel departments, but the report does not discuss this week.

findings.title: Gulf Coast comparison is thin
findings.text: Only one other store in the Gulf Coast region (Store 34) was available for comparison. It was flagged in Furniture, Cameras, Plus & Maternity, Bras / Lingerie, Licensed Sports Apparel, Horticulture and Hosiery, so it offers only limited support.

departments.what_supports_it: Store 4 was at $5,234 against an $8,381 forecast (-37.5%), while other stores were at a median of -13.9%. Furniture was below forecast at 29 of 36 other stores, and the Beige Book noted a pickup in furniture sales in Boston, which is outside this store's district.
Store 4 was at -26.4% against a median of -12.6% at other stores, and 38 of 44 other stores were below forecast. The ML team's notes list a recent decline and a seasonal decline.
Store 4 was at -21.7%, close to the -17.7% threshold. Other stores had a median of -5.4%, and 27 of 37 were below forecast. Bedding is part of the Home category described in the 10-K.
Store 4 was at -25.6%, while other stores had a median of -14.1%. The ML team's notes say the model was too high at 67.6% of other stores.
Store 4 was at -33.2%, but other stores had a median of +11.1%. This suggests a drop specific to this store, possibly from local stock or display issues.
Store 4 was at -36.5%, while other stores had a median of +6.5%. Like Cameras, this looks specific to this store.

report.not_found: No outside factor explains these drops: the week had no holiday, fuel and temperature changed little, and unemployment was flat, and no report discusses this store's departments that week.
next_steps: Check stock on hand and recent deliveries for Furniture, Lawn & Garden, Horticulture and Bedding.
Check whether Cameras, Boyswear and Hosiery had stockouts, display changes or pricing changes that week.
Check staffing levels for the week in the Home and Apparel areas.
Check for local events or new competitors near the store in the week of Sep 28, 2012.
Check the sales entries for Cameras, Hosiery and Boyswear for possible data-entry errors.
data_needed: Department-level inventory and delivery records for Store 4 covering the flagged weeks.
Department-level markdown records (the $17,027 recorded this week is store-wide and cannot be tied to a department).
Sales for Gulf Coast stores beyond Store 34 to test whether the Home pattern holds regionally.
Local competitor openings or promotions near Store 4 for the week ending Sep 28, 2012.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: We have a comprehensive marketing plan that's designed to ensure we have the number one share of voice this season. We're increasing our presence across the traditional media channels, with big increases in TV and radio. We have some great holiday commercials lined up that will be fun, but more importantly, reinforce our price leadership. Additionally, we'll generate over 2 billion impressions across social media this holiday, more than three times last year's total.

Retail Sales Retail sales grew slightly over the reporting period and were up from a year ago. Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel. Sales growth in the Eleventh District remained stronger than the nation, on average, according to two large retailers. Retailers expect a seasonal pickup in demand in the fourth quarter, although sales will likely be down from last year. Automobile sales were mostly flat since the last report, but were up from year ago levels. Inventories were lighter than desired. Contacts said political uncertainty was hampering consumer confidence, and outlooks were cautious.

report.summary: Several flagged departments were below the ML forecast at many stores in the same week, not just at Store 6. Walmart overall was also below the ML forecast that week, and the Dallas Fed report describes apparel and cosmetics sales as strong, so no report explains these drops directly. The store-level markdown figure cannot be tied to any department.

findings.title: Dept 5 and 36 below forecast chain-wide
findings.text: In the week ending Aug 31, 2012, 41 of 44 other stores were below the ML forecast for Dept 5 Media & Gaming, and 31 of 36 were below it for Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear. This points to a wider cause shared across stores, though the cause is not verified.

findings.title: Texas stores also below forecast in several departments
findings.text: In Texas, 10 of 10 other stores were below the ML forecast for Dept 33 Girlswear and for Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear, with 7 and 9 of them flagged respectively. Store 6 is part of this regional pattern in these departments.

findings.title: Walmart overall below forecast that week
findings.text: All 45 stores that week sold $47,131,887 against a $48,409,634 forecast (-2.6%), with 35 of 45 stores below the forecast. For the quarter, Walmart U.S. comparable sales were reported at +1.5%, so the week was softer than the quarter as a whole.

findings.title: Dallas report describes apparel as strong
findings.text: The Dallas Fed Beige Book of Aug 29, 2012 says: "Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel." This describes the district in general and does not explain the drops at Store 6, which are in some of these same categories.

findings.title: Some outside changes that week
findings.text: Local fuel was $3.64/gal against $3.53 in the prior 4-week median, and temperature was 84°F against 87°F. There was no holiday and unemployment was unchanged at 5.7%. These changes are possible contributors, but no report links them to these departments.

findings.title: ML team notes on Dept 5 and 49
findings.text: The ML team's notes say that for Dept 5 the forecast was above actual at 93.2% of other stores, and for Dept 49 Optical at 80.7% of other stores. These are the ML team's own notes and do not explain why sales fell at Store 6.

departments.what_supports_it: Store 6 was -20.2% against the ML forecast, and 41 of 44 other stores were also below it that week. This is the largest pattern shared across stores.
Store 6 was -45.6% against the ML forecast, the largest gap in the flagged list, and 31 of 36 other stores were also below. Texas stores were below in 10 of 10 cases.
Store 6 was -29.9% against the ML forecast, and all 10 Texas stores were below. Across all stores the median gap was -10.3%, so the drop is stronger at Store 6 than the typical store.
Store 6 was -25.3% against the ML forecast, while the all-store median was -1.2%. Most of the drop appears specific to Store 6, and the Dallas report does not mention boys' apparel weakness.

report.not_found: No report, outside factor or other store data was found that explains the drops at Store 6 in these departments, and no store-level markdown can be linked to any department.
next_steps: Check stock on hand and recent deliveries for Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear and Dept 33 Girlswear, since these are the largest shared drops.

Check staffing levels and schedules in Entertainment and Apparel for the week ending Aug 31, 2012.
Check for local competitor sales, promotions or events near Store 6 that week.
Check the data entry for the 10 flagged departments, including any sales recorded under the wrong department.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book.
