passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Our apparel business posted a low single-digit comp increase, making this the third straight quarter of positive comps. The consistency of our apparel business and focus on basics, especially in kids, ladies, and men's, continues to drive growth, despite the impact of a warm October across much of the country. We have worked hard on improving item quality, focusing on the elements that our customers appreciate, and are optimistic that our current trend will continue into the holiday season.

Economic activity in the Twelfth District grew at a modest pace during the reporting period of mid-August through late-September. Upward price pressures remained limited overall, and upward wage pressures remained muted. Sales of retail items rose slightly, and demand for most business and consumer services gained further on net. District manufacturing activity edged up. Agricultural output was mostly steady, while activity continued to trend up for providers of energy resources. Home demand in the District showed continued signs of improvement, and demand for commercial real estate was mainly stable. Financial institutions reported overall loan demand was unchanged or up somewhat on balance.

report.summary: Store 28 was below the ML forecast in 59 of 69 departments that week, and several flagged departments also fell across Walmart and the West Coast region. Stationery and Lawn & Garden show the clearest broad pattern, while Seafood and Fabrics & Crafts look more specific to this store. No report or outside factor directly explains these drops.

findings.title: Most stores below forecast that week
findings.text: Across Walmart that week, 36 of 45 stores were below the ML forecast. In Dept 3 Stationery, 43 of 44 other stores were below the ML forecast, so this store's drop is part of a wider pattern.

findings.title: Stationery and Lawn & Garden drop across the region
findings.text: In the West Coast (PADD 5) region, all 5 other stores were below the ML forecast in Dept 3 Stationery and in Dept 16 Lawn & Garden. Four of the five Lawn & Garden stores were flagged by the ML team.

findings.title: Seafood and Fabrics drop look local
findings.text: Store 28's Seafood sales were $5,924 against an ML forecast of $8,915. Other stores were only a median of -5.5% below forecast in that department, and Store 28 ranks lowest of 42. Fabrics & Crafts was also far below its forecast here while most other stores were close to forecast.

findings.title: Outside factors show little change
findings.text: The week had no holiday, fuel was $4.13/gal against $4.07, temperature was 84°F against 89°F, and unemployment was 10.9% against 10.9%. None of these clearly matches the size of the drops in these departments.

findings.title: Fed report describes slight retail growth
findings.text: The Fed's Oct 10, 2012 report on the San Francisco district, covering mid-August through late-September, said "Sales of retail items rose slightly" and that "Home demand in the District showed continued signs of improvement." This is general district context and does not point to any specific store drop.

findings.title: ML team notes a seasonal pattern
findings.text: The ML team's notes describe Lawn & Garden as having a seasonal decline, with a same-season earlier-year median of $6,760 against this week's -32.3%. The notes also say the model was too high at 95.5% of other stores.

A major retail chain reports that sales in the region were sluggish in August and especially in September, running well below comparable 2011 levels. Some of the weakness is attributed to unseasonably mild weather, which dampened sales of seasonal merchandise. A major mall in upstate New York describes sales activity as "stagnant", with sales flat to down slightly from a year ago in August and September. findings.title: Regional report cites mild weather
findings.text: The Federal Reserve Beige Book of Oct 10, 2012 says "Some of the weakness is attributed to unseasonably mild weather, which dampened sales of seasonal merchandise." It describes New York sales as "flat to down slightly" in August and September. This describes the region in general, not this store.

findings.title: Store-wide drop across departments
findings.text: At Store 27, 54 of 69 departments were below the ML forecast, and the store as a whole was $1,527,276 against a forecast of $1,624,819 (-6.0%). Across all 45 stores that week the total was -1.9%.

findings.title: ML team notes on model fit

departments.what_supports_it: This is the largest dollar gap, at $4,477 (-22.1%). 27 of 37 other stores were also below the ML forecast in this department, with a median of -5.4%, so the gap is larger here than at most stores.

29 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast with a median of -13.9%, and all three other New York stores were below too. The Beige Book notes a pickup in furniture sales in Boston, which is not this region.

This is the most widespread pattern: 38 of 44 other stores were below forecast. The regional report on mild weather dampening seasonal merchandise fits this category, though no report names Lawn & Garden directly.
9 of 10 other stores were below the ML forecast with a median of -8.8%, so this is a broad pattern. This store's -43.4% is the largest percentage gap among the flagged departments.

Peers did not show a broad drop: the median of other stores was -0.7%, and only 20 of 39 were below forecast. This store's -40.0% is therefore more specific to this store, so store-side checks matter most here.
22 of 33 other stores were below the ML forecast with a median of -4.7%, and this store's -20.6% is only just above the -20.2% threshold. This suggests a smaller, more typical shortfall.

passages.text: Petrochemicals producers noted Gulf Coast chemical production was up slightly, but uncertainty cautioned firms' outlooks. Gulf Coast refiners said they were operating at rates above 90 percent, and strong export demand was keeping inventories from building. Retail Sales Retailers said demand was mixed over the past six weeks. Sales in the Eleventh District continued to outperform the nation, according to two national retailers. Contacts said the loss in sales resulting from Hurricane Sandy was temporary and would not impact holiday spending. Outlooks through year-end were mixed.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

Consumer Spending and Tourism District contacts indicated demand and sales were up slightly in October compared with September. Most retailers felt that consumer confidence is improving as they head into the holiday season, which led to expectations that sales would improve over last year's results. Retailers anticipate a healthy holiday season and most shared plans to hire the same amount of seasonal staff compared with last year, although there were some contacts that anticipate hiring a bit more help over the holidays than they did in 2011. Automobile dealers continued to report strong sales growth, albeit a bit less robust than earlier in the year. Low interest rates, aging vehicles, available credit, and the popularity of new fuel-efficient models were factors cited as driving growth.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript

High-tech manufacturers said sales growth slowed modestly over the reporting period. Most contacts attributed the slowdown to weakened international demand and lower forecasts for world economic growth. Weaker demand was noted across a broad range of products, including industrial, computers and communications infrastructure. Contacts expect demand to remain weak through year-end. Demand for paper products increased in line with normal seasonal patterns. Food producers noted increased business over the last thirty days due to a slight pickup in consumer demand. Reports from most transportation equipment manufacturers were mixed; aviation manufacturing orders were down slightly while other firms noted flat to increased activity.

Forward-looking statements This release contains statements as to Walmart management's forecasts of the company's earnings per share for the fiscal quarter and fiscal year to end Jan. 31, 2013 (and certain assumptions underlying such forecasts), and management's expectations regarding the comparable store sales of the Walmart U.S. segment and comparable club sales, excluding fuel, of the Sam's Club segment of the company for the 13-week period from Oct. 27, 2012 through Jan. 25, 2013, and management's expectations that the Walmart U.S. operating segment will have strong performance through Thanksgiving weekend, that the company believes are "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, as amended.

report.summary: Several flagged departments were also below the ML forecast at many other stores that week, most clearly Sporting Goods and Licensed Sports Apparel, so a shared category pattern is possible. Store 4's drops in Sporting Goods and Apparel are deeper than the typical store's. Wireless Services and Optical look more local to this store, and no store-side record was found that explains any of the drops.

findings.title: Sporting goods fell at many stores
findings.text: In the same department at other stores that week, 36 of 44 were also below the ML forecast, with a median of -8.1%. This store was at -28.3%, which is deeper than the typical store. The ML team's notes say the model ran too high at 81.8% of other stores.

findings.title: Apparel and domestics also softer widely
findings.text: Licensed Sports Apparel was below the ML forecast at 25 of 36 other stores, with a median of -22.8%; this store was at -23.5%. Domestics / Bath was below the ML forecast at 31 of 40 other stores, with a median of -13.4%; this store was at -21.2%.

findings.title: Region shows same sporting goods and apparel drops
findings.text: The one other store in the Gulf Coast region was also flagged in Sporting Goods at -28.6% and in Licensed Sports Apparel at -27.9%. With only one comparison store, this shows a local pattern in the region but is not a broad test.

findings.title: Week-wide conditions were mild, possibly weather
findings.text: Walmart overall was -0.4% against forecast that week, with 27 of 45 stores below. Temperature was 57°F against 69°F the prior weeks' median, and fuel was $3.60 per gallon against $3.69, so the fuel price fell rather than rose. A national Beige Book from Oct 10, 2012 said that "rising gasoline prices" and "weather" were among factors affecting sales, though that is general context, not this store's data.

findings.title: Wireless and optical drops look local
findings.text: Store 4 was -1.7% overall, with 37 of 71 departments below forecast. Wireless Services was at -38.2% here, but 9 of 25 other stores were below forecast in that department, with a median of +18.6%. Optical was at -30.4% here, while the median at other stores was +2.0%.

departments.what_supports_it: Most other stores were also below forecast in this department that week (36 of 44, median -8.1%), though this store's -28.3% is deeper. The ML team's notes say the same department was -2.2% against the same season in earlier years, which is a mixed signal.
25 of 36 other stores were below forecast in this department, with a median of -22.8%, and the one regional comparison store was flagged at -27.9%. The ML team's notes describe a recent decline.

31 of 40 other stores were below forecast, with a median of -13.4%, so a broad softness is possible. This store's -21.2% is close to the typical drop elsewhere, and the ML team's notes say the model ran too high at most stores.
Other stores generally did not drop here (median +18.6%), so the -38.2% looks specific to this store. The ML team's notes say it was -67.4% against the same season in earlier years.
Other stores were typically flat to up (median +2.0%), so the -30.4% here looks local. The ML team's notes describe a seasonal decline and a recent decline.
5 of 6 other stores were below forecast, with a median of -32.4%, so a shared pattern is possible. The department is small, with $30 actual against $55 forecast here, and its name is unresolved.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

report.summary: Store 31 sold $1,373,641 against a $1,438,399 ML forecast for the week ending Aug 31, 2012 (-4.5%), and 10 departments were flagged. The same departments were also below the ML forecast at many other Walmart stores, especially in Texas, so the drops look shared rather than local. Nothing found so far explains why this store's drops are larger than most other stores'.

findings.title: Same departments down at many stores
findings.text: Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear was below the ML forecast at 31 of 36 other stores that week, and Dept 99 Store Supplies at all 14 other stores. Store 31's drops in these departments are part of a wider pattern.

findings.title: Texas stores show the same pattern
findings.text: In Texas, 10 of 10 other stores were below the ML forecast in Dept 33 Girlswear and in Dept 36, and 12 of 13 in Dept 5 Media & Gaming. The drops are broad across the region, not just at Store 31.

findings.title: Store-wide sales slightly below forecast
findings.text: Store 31 was below the ML forecast in 47 of 69 departments that week, a store-wide gap of -4.5% against Walmart's -2.6%. Store-wide markdowns were $47,982, but the records do not show which departments they touched, so they cannot be linked to these drops.

findings.title: Weather and fuel prices moved this week
findings.text: No holiday fell in this week. Temperature was 84°F against 88°F in the prior four-week median, and local fuel was $3.64/gal against $3.53. The Beige Book notes that rising gasoline prices and weather were factors affecting sales in general, though it does not name these departments.

findings.title: Dallas district report on inventory

report.summary: Store 6 sold $1,513,228 against a $1,623,605 ML forecast (-6.8%) in the week ending Jul 27, 2012. Many other stores also fell below the forecast in the same departments, so the flagged drops look at least partly shared, not local. No store-side cause is shown in the data; the reasons below are possible explanations only.

findings.title: Entertainment drops seen at many stores
findings.text: Dept 5 Media & Gaming was below the ML forecast at 37 of 44 other stores that week, and at 10 of 13 other Texas stores. Store 6's drop of -24.7% is in the middle of that group.

findings.title: Apparel drop was widespread that week
findings.text: Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear was below the ML forecast at 35 of 36 other stores, with a median of -36.9%. Store 6 was at -40.5%, close to the typical drop for this department.

findings.title: Store 6 softness spans most departments
findings.text: 55 of Store 6's 70 departments were below the ML forecast that week, so the shortfall is not limited to the 6 flagged departments. Across all 45 stores, 43 were below forecast, a total of -5.0%.

findings.title: Walmart cites entertainment category trends
findings.text: On the Aug 16, 2012 earnings call, Walmart said "industry trends in electronics continue to impact the broader entertainment category." This is Walmart-wide context, not a finding about Store 6.

findings.title: Weather and fuel changed; no holiday
findings.text: The week had no holiday, temperature was 86°F against 82°F in the prior four-week median, and fuel was $3.41/gal against $3.27. These may bear on apparel and seasonal departments, but no report ties them to Store 6's numbers.

departments.what_supports_it: This was the largest gap, and 37 of 44 other stores also fell below forecast in this department, pointing to a wider cause. The Walmart earnings call cites entertainment category trends.
35 of 36 other stores fell below forecast, a shared pattern across the chain. The week's warmer weather may be a possible factor, but no report links it to this department.
30 of 36 other stores were below forecast, with a median of -10.4%. Store 6's -21.4% is consistent with a shared entertainment-category drop.
13 of 22 other stores were below forecast, and 10 of those were flagged. The drop at Store 6 (-45.4%) is larger than the typical store, so local causes cannot be ruled out.
Only 19 of 35 other stores were below forecast, with a median of -0.8%. Store 6's -24.9% is well below that, so this drop looks more local than the others.
The actual was $6 against a $72 forecast, a very small amount. Its unit and name are unresolved, so it may be a data-entry issue; the drop is shared by 4 of 6 other stores, but the evidence is weak.

passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Our apparel business posted a low single-digit comp increase, making this the third straight quarter of positive comps. The consistency of our apparel business and focus on basics, especially in kids, ladies, and men's, continues to drive growth, despite the impact of a warm October across much of the country. We have worked hard on improving item quality, focusing on the elements that our customers appreciate, and are optimistic that our current trend will continue into the holiday season.

Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has firmed somewhat since the last report. Two major retail chains report that sales in the region were on plan in July and ahead of plan in early August. Similarly a major retail mall in upstate New York reports some firming in sales, as well as shopper traffic, in July and early August, following lackluster business in May and June. Retail prices continue to be described as steady--including apparel prices, which had previously been expected to drift down with the retreat in cotton prices earlier this year. Stores in New York City have performed on par or modestly better than those in the rest of the region. Inventories are generally said to be at or slightly above desired levels.

BENTONVILLE, Ark., Nov. 15, 2012 — Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. (NYSE: WMT) today reported financial results for the quarter ended Oct. 31, 2012. Net sales for the third quarter of fiscal 2013 were $113.2 billion, an increase of 3.4 percent from $109.5 billion in the third quarter last year. Net sales for this quarter included a negative currency exchange rate impact of approximately $1.7 billion. Without the currency impact, net sales would have been $114.9 billion. Membership and other income increased 2.1 percent to $725 million. Total revenue was $113.9 billion, an increase of 3.4 percent from last year. See additional information at the end of this release regarding non-GAAP measures.

report.summary: Apparel departments show the widest pattern in this week. Outerwear & Swimwear sold below the ML forecast at 35 of 36 other stores, and this store's drop was the second largest of the flagged departments. Store 27 as a whole was $1,704,696 against an ML forecast of $1,789,823 (-4.8%), and the week ending Aug 3, 2012 had no holiday and a cooler temperature than the prior weeks. These are possible contributing conditions only; no cause has been verified.

findings.title: Outerwear and swimwear weak across stores
findings.text: In the week ending Aug 3, 2012, 35 of 36 other stores sold below the ML forecast in Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear, with a median of -44.9%. Store 27 was at -75.5%, so this is a wide pattern that is deeper here.

findings.title: New York stores also below in outerwear
findings.text: All 3 other New York State stores were below the ML forecast in Outerwear & Swimwear that week, and all 3 were flagged. Optical (Dept 49) also fell below the forecast at all 3 other New York stores, while the all-store median for Optical was +4.7%, so the Optical pattern looks regional rather than national.

findings.title: Cooler week and higher fuel price
findings.text: The week had no holiday. Temperature was 75°F against a prior four-week median of 79°F, and local fuel was $3.82/gal against $3.71. A cooler week could plausibly reduce demand for outerwear and swimwear, but this link is not confirmed by any store record.

findings.title: Regional report: apparel prices steady
findings.text: The Federal Reserve Beige Book dated Aug 29, 2012, which was published after this week, says "Retail prices continue to be described as steady" and notes that sales in New York firmed in July and early August. It covers the whole New York Fed District, not Store 27, and does not mention outerwear, swimwear or this store.

findings.title: Drop spread across store's departments
findings.text: 47 of Store 27's 68 departments sold below the ML forecast that week, and the store total was -4.8%. Walmart overall was -0.4%, with 20 of 45 stores below the forecast, so the store's shortfall is larger than the chain-wide one.

findings.title: ML team notes on apparel trends
findings.text: The ML team's notes say the model was too high at 58.3% of other stores for Ladieswear and at 97.2% for Outerwear & Swimwear. Its notes also list a recent decline for Ladieswear and a seasonal decline for Outerwear & Swimwear. These are the ML team's own notes, not verified causes.

departments.what_supports_it: This was the largest gap at -24.0%, ranked number 1 from the bottom of 37 stores. Only 21 of 36 other stores were below the forecast, with a median of -1.4%, so the drop is mostly specific to this store.
35 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast (median -44.9%), and 3 of 3 New York stores were flagged. This is the clearest department-wide pattern in this week.
Store 27 was at -40.5%, number 3 from the bottom. 28 of 36 other stores were below the forecast (median -15.3%), but only 1 of 3 New York stores was, so the pattern is broad but not regional.
Store 27 was at -26.6%. Nationally the median was +4.7%, but all 3 other New York stores were below the forecast, 2 of them flagged, which points to a possible regional factor.

plan.why: The three largest dollar gaps are Pharmacy ($8,574), Bedding ($1,832) and Cameras ($916), so the searches target what Walmart reported for those categories in FY2013 Q3, the Texas retail and consumer picture in the Dallas Fed district, and the summer heat and fuel conditions that week.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported modest increases in retail spending on a year-over-year basis, but many reported slower growth in recent months compared with earlier in the year; however, Boston and Cleveland reported sales as flat, and New York cited softer sales. There were a few reports that high summer temperatures negatively affected sales. Sales of big-ticket household goods were strong in the Richmond, Chicago, Kansas City, and Dallas Districts, while sales were reportedly flat for home furnishings and major appliances in the San Francisco District. Boston reported that sales for furniture and electronics had slowed, and retailers in the New York District reported that home goods sales were weak. Reports from luxury-goods retailers were mixed.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Health and wellness continues to be a key traffic driver as well and overall delivered a mid single-digit comp increase. Hearing aid centers achieved double-digit comps for the quarter. We had mid single-digit comps in OTC and low single-digit comps in prescriptions. Like Walmart U.S., the recent availability of popular prescriptions that have moved from branded to generic status negatively impacted overall sales, but drove profitability and unit volume. Rx script count was up mid single-digits, and we expect this trend to continue.

Retail Sales Retail sales increased but the pace of growth decelerated slightly compared to earlier in the year. Sales of apparel, bedding, household items, and small furniture fared well. Discount retailers said sales of food and sundries continued to perform the strongest. Overall sales growth in the Eleventh District continued to outpace the nation, on average, according to three large retailers. Outlooks are cautiously optimistic and contacts say it appears as if the environment has improved slightly for the consumer. Automobile sales continued to grow at a steady pace. Inventories were at desired levels and prices remained stable. Auto dealers expect sales growth to continue at the same pace through year end.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.text: The forward-looking statements also discuss management's expectations for Walmart's Sam's Club operating segment: that the trend of increased certain prescription drugs sales will continue for the segment; that inflation will have a lesser effect on revenues in future periods; and regarding the number of new clubs that the segment will open in the third quarter of fiscal year 2013. The forward-looking statements also discuss other goals and objectives of Walmart and the anticipation and expectations of Walmart and its management as to other future occurrences, trends, and results. All of these forward-looking statements are subject to risks, uncertainties and other factors, domestically and

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Comparable store and club sales in the U.S., including fuel, increased 2.4% and 1.6% in fiscal 2013 and 2012 , respectively, when compared to the previous fiscal year. U.S. comparable store and club sales increased during fiscal 2013 as a result of improved average ticket and an increase in customer traffic. U.S. comparable store sales increased during fiscal 2012 primarily due to an increase in average ticket, partially offset by a decline in traffic, while comparable club sales were higher due to a larger member base driving increased traffic, as well as a broader assortment of items. As we continue to add new stores and clubs in the U.S., we do so with an understanding that additional stores and clubs may take sales away from existing units. We estimate the negative impact on comparable store and club sales as a result of opening new stores and clubs was approximately 0.7% in fiscal 2013 and 0.8% in fiscal 2012 .

report.summary: Store 21 sold $692,959 against a $723,002 ML forecast (-4.2%), with 12 departments flagged, while Walmart overall for the week was -0.4%. The pharmacy and bedding drops look local to this store, while the apparel, horticulture and some grocery drops are shared across Texas and many other stores.

findings.title: Pharmacy drop looks specific to this store
findings.text: Dept 38 Pharmacy (Rx) was $8,574 below the ML forecast here (-26.2%). Most other stores' pharmacy sales were near or above their forecasts (median +2.0%), and no other Texas store was flagged in this department.

findings.title: Walmart report links prescription sales to generics
findings.text: A Walmart earnings call from Aug 16, 2012 says "the recent availability of popular prescriptions that have moved from branded to generic status negatively impacted overall sales." This is Walmart-wide context, not a finding about Store 21.

findings.title: Apparel and horticulture fell across Texas
findings.text: Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear was below forecast at 35 of 36 stores (median -45.8%), and 9 of 10 Texas stores were below. Dept 56 Horticulture was below forecast at 34 of 38 stores, and all 11 Texas stores were below. This points to a shared category or seasonal pattern.

findings.title: Heat is a possible shared factor
findings.text: Temperature was 92°F this week against 85°F in the prior four-week median. A Federal Reserve report from Jul 18, 2012 says "There were a few reports that high summer temperatures negatively affected sales." This is general context and does not confirm a cause here.

findings.title: Bedding drop is local, against a regional trend
findings.text: Dept 22 Bedding was above forecast at most other stores (median +9.6%), but Store 21 was -25.9%. A Dallas Fed report from Jul 18, 2012 says "Sales of apparel, bedding, household items, and small furniture fared well." The report does not match this store's bedding result.

departments.what_supports_it: The drop is at this store only, and a Walmart report ties prescription sales to generic availability. The ML notes list a seasonal decline for this department, but earlier-year seasonal sales were not verified here.
Most other stores were above forecast in this department, so the drop looks local. The Dallas Fed report describes bedding sales as doing well in the district.
Nearly every store was below forecast, and the ML notes list recent and seasonal declines. The Texas drop is shared, and the heat report is general.
All 11 other Texas stores were below forecast, and 34 of 38 stores overall were below. This suggests a shared category pattern.
Many stores were below forecast, and 17 were also flagged by the ML team. Store 21's drop is in line with the broader pattern.

report.not_found: No store-side record of stock levels, staffing, pricing, displays or local competitors was found in the data, and there was no holiday this week.
next_steps: Check pharmacy stock and deliveries for the weeks ending Jul 27 and Aug 3, 2012, especially generic substitutions.
Compare pharmacy prescription counts with the store's sales for the same weeks.
Check whether apparel and horticulture displays, clearance placement or stock levels changed this week.
Review the store-wide markdown timing against these departments, without treating it as a department-level cause.
Ask staff whether Dept 22 Bedding had a stock, display or recording issue.
Check for local events, weather effects or competitor promotions near Store 21 that week.
data_needed: Weekly pharmacy script counts and generic share for Store 21 and nearby stores
Department-level markdowns or price changes (not currently available, since markdowns are store-level only)
Store-level stock and delivery records by department for the week ending Aug 3, 2012
Local competitor pricing or promotion records for Texas stores that week

plan.why: Dept_26, dept_20, and dept_71 have the largest dollar gaps ($3,148, $2,429, $2,299), and the search should test whether category-level weakness or regional conditions explain them, while noting that the chain-wide dept_26 and dept_71 declines are small, so the store-specific gap may not be explained by them alone.

passages.text: During the 13-week period, both comp ticket and traffic rose for Walmart U.S., and both grocery and general merchandise had positive comp sales. "Our comp sales momentum continued through the second quarter, with July being one of our strongest months. All three geographic business units and all store formats had positive comp sales. Customers are responding to our continued focus on providing the right assortment at everyday low prices and are shopping the entire store," said Bill Simon, Walmart U.S. president and chief executive officer. "We have a powerful strategy and I'm confident in our ability to deliver sustained strong financial performance." For the 4-5-4 period from July 28 through October 26, Walmart U.S. expects comparable store sales to range from 1.0 percent to 3.0 percent.

Natural Resources and Agriculture Contacts reported a renewed increase in production at Gulf Coast refineries because of recent closures along the East Coast. An increase in demand for crude oil and oil products, along with the Gulf Coast seeing particularly high demand for diesel fuels and other distillates, has helped to support refined product prices. Recent rains improved conditions in many parts of the District. Compared with the same time last year, prices paid to farmers for soybeans, corn, oranges, beef, hogs, and broilers were up while cotton was down. Although beef prices have increased over the last year, contacts reported that both the drought and high feed prices have resulted in lower prices paid to farmers on a month-over-month basis.

passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Home, including seasonal categories, had a low single-digit positive comp. Our continued focus on basics, supported by strong item merchandising and a refined assortment, drove strong performance in the quarter. Indoor living, led by cooking and dining, again performed well, as most departments posted an increased comp versus the first quarter. Back-to-school and back-to-college shopping is well under way. Our stores were ready to serve shoppers early in the season, and we're pleased with the results. Season to date, key back-to-school apparel categories are up 7.0 percent. Within home, we're seeing strong performance in college essentials like bedding and bath.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.text: In our consumables business where we continue to focus on price, we had solid increases in unit sales. Table-top and personal paper categories had mid single-digit increases. Our recent launch of the new Member's Mark paper plate is outselling comparable branded items and is creating additional margin that allows us to price more aggressively. Tobacco sales, which remain important for convenience store owners, were a drag on overall comp sales for the quarter, but that reduction helped drive a merchandising mix that was a positive to profit. Technology, entertainment and office achieved low single-digit comps. Performance was strong in portable electronics, including tablets, but challenged by continued softness in video games, movies, and books.

report.summary: Store 4 sold $2,048,614 in the week ending Jul 27, 2012, against a $2,161,194 ML forecast (-5.2%), with 7 departments flagged. passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported modest increases in retail spending on a year-over-year basis, but many reported slower growth in recent months compared with earlier in the year; however, Boston and Cleveland reported sales as flat, and New York cited softer sales. There were a few reports that high summer temperatures negatively affected sales. Sales of big-ticket household goods were strong in the Richmond, Chicago, Kansas City, and Dallas Districts, while sales were reportedly flat for home furnishings and major appliances in the San Francisco District. Boston reported that sales for furniture and electronics had slowed, and retailers in the New York District reported that home goods sales were weak. Reports from luxury-goods retailers were mixed.

passages.section: Now, I'll turn it over to Doug for the International update. Doug …
passages.text: Despite a difficult consumer environment and the wettest weather on record, ASDA gained market share in the second quarter, according to the Kantar Worldwide Panel Total Till Roll for the 12 weeks ending July 8. Excluding fuel, net sales grew 3.2 percent. Comparable sales, excluding fuel, increased 0.7 percent, with ticket up 2.6 percent, and traffic decreasing 1.9 percent. The strongest performances were in grocery, apparel and electronics. In addition, our online business in the U.K. improved its already strong performance, with sales growth of 22.1 percent in the quarter.

Net sales for the Walmart U.S. segment increased 3.8% and 4.8% during the three and six months ended July 31, 2012, respectively, when compared to the same periods in the previous year. The increases in net sales were primarily due to increases in comparable store sales of 1.9% and 3.1% as a result of improved ticket and traffic for the three and six months ended July 31, 2012, respectively, combined with year-over-year growth in retail square feet of 1.9%. Our focus on expanded merchandise assortment and price leadership drove our sales performance. Gross profit rate declined 20 and 22 basis points during the three and six months ended July 31, 2012, respectively, compared to the same periods in the previous year.

Retail Trade and Services Retail sales expanded a bit further overall. Respondents in general indicated that sales strengthened somewhat in July compared with softness in May and June. Performance was stronger for discount chains than traditional department stores, particularly for online sales. At grocery stores, extensive bargain hunting by shoppers caused sales revenues to weaken a bit. The pace of auto sales slowed somewhat compared with the prior reporting period, although it remained significantly above the pace from the same period last year. Used vehicles have been in short supply, raising their trade-in values and helping to spur sales of new vehicles.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported modest increases in retail spending on a year-over-year basis, but many reported slower growth in recent months compared with earlier in the year; however, Boston and Cleveland reported sales as flat, and New York cited softer sales. Sales of big-ticket household goods were strong in the Richmond, Chicago, Kansas City, and Dallas Districts, while sales were reportedly flat for home furnishings and major appliances in the San Francisco District. passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Most of our merchandising areas again delivered solid performance, though industry trends in electronics continue to impact the broader entertainment category. We're seeing market share growth across grocery and health & wellness. You can expect to hear more about market share and how we're using Nielsen data during our annual analyst meeting in October.

Retail Sales Retail sales grew slightly over the reporting period and were up from a year ago. Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel. Sales growth in the Eleventh District remained stronger than the nation, on average, according to two large retailers. Retailers expect a seasonal pickup in demand in the fourth quarter, although sales will likely be down from last year. Automobile sales were mostly flat since the last report, but were up from year ago levels. Inventories were lighter than desired. Contacts said political uncertainty was hampering consumer confidence, and outlooks were cautious.

passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: The continued strong industry deflation led to a low single-digit negative comp for entertainment. Within wireless, a broader assortment resulted in double-digit comp sales growth, as customers continue to look at Walmart as a wireless destination. In media and gaming, we're well positioned for a very strong release schedule throughout the fourth quarter. Top releases like Halo and Call of Duty drove customers into our store over the last several weeks. Layaway drove a great deal of interest in toys, including toy construction, educational toys, ride-ons, and bicycles. We're well stocked in this season's must-have toys, and will be able to delight our younger customers all season long.

Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has firmed somewhat since the last report. Two major retail chains report that sales in the region were on plan in July and ahead of plan in early August. Similarly a major retail mall in upstate New York reports some firming in sales, as well as shopper traffic, in July and early August, following lackluster business in May and June. Retail prices continue to be described as steady--including apparel prices, which had previously been expected to drift down with the retreat in cotton prices earlier this year. Stores in New York City have performed on par or modestly better than those in the rest of the region. Inventories are generally said to be at or slightly above desired levels.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most District merchants reported that sales growth remained slow in September. Discount retail operations outperformed traditional department stores. Most retailers projected continued soft growth in sales through the end of 2012. Contacts in the auto industry reported that strong sales levels were maintained in September.

passages.text: Although we are pleased with the positive results, we are disappointed that comp sales were below our guidance. This miss was driven by several factors. The combination of inflation and deflation across multiple categories affected comp sales. Inflation in some categories led members to trade down. Deflation in other categories came faster and deeper late in the quarter, with October being the lowest inflation we have seen in some time. Finally, our business members continue to experience economic pressure and uncertainty, which led to slower growth in business member traffic. We anticipate this softening could remain a headwind in the fourth quarter.

Retail and Tourism First District retail contacts offer a very mixed take on economic conditions in the region. Demand remains strong for adult clothing, but spending on durable items such as furniture and electronics continues to be lower than earlier in the year. Some companies cite disappointing sales during the last six weeks, while others report some upside surprises. Sales results range from low single-digit declines to high single-digit increases compared with a year earlier. Some contacts say that consumer sentiment has become more negative, while others observe that consumers are "coming back." Retailers note wholesale prices remain flat so they are holding selling prices steady. Respondents still express uncertainty about the direction of the U.S. economy and say they expect little improvement over the next six to eight months.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

During the 13-week period, both comp ticket and traffic rose for Walmart U.S., and both grocery and general merchandise had positive comp sales. "Our comp sales momentum continued through the second quarter, with July being one of our strongest months. All three geographic business units and all store formats had positive comp sales. Customers are responding to our continued focus on providing the right assortment at everyday low prices and are shopping the entire store," said Bill Simon, Walmart U.S. president and chief executive officer. "We have a powerful strategy and I'm confident in our ability to deliver sustained strong financial performance." For the 4-5-4 period from July 28 through October 26, Walmart U.S. expects comparable store sales to range from 1.0 percent to 3.0 percent.

passages.section: Walmart U.S. Neighborhood Markets and Other Small Formats
passages.text: • Apparel includes apparel for women, girls, men, boys and infants, shoes, jewelry and accessories; and • Home includes home furnishings, housewares and small appliances, bedding, home décor, outdoor living and horticulture.

"We were pleased that our constant currency sales and operating income were both up approximately 7 percent for the third quarter," said Doug McMillon, president and CEO of Walmart International. "We gained market share in almost all of our markets, indicating that our underlying business is performing well. We are working hard to improve execution where it's needed, and we're ready with great merchandise and price investments for the fourth quarter." (Walmart) reported third quarter diluted earnings per share from continuing operations of $1.08, within guidance of $1.04 to $1.09. This was an 11.3 percent increase from the $0.97 per share reported for the third quarter last year.

Wages and Prices Price inflation was limited for most final goods and services during the reporting period. Prices increased for some energy items, mainly crude oil, retail gasoline, and electricity, but natural gas prices remained near historic lows. Contacts also noted price increases for assorted food commodities, particularly grains, although meat prices reportedly have leveled off for the time being. For most products and services, vigorous competition among firms and cost-conscious purchasing behavior by consumers kept price inflation in check.

passages.text: Demand for paper products held steady, and contacts said they expect modest sales growth for the year. Food producers said sales activity increased over the past six weeks and orders were up significantly from year-ago levels. One food manufacturer reported adding several new workers in part due to strong demand. Automobile and aviation equipment manufacturers said demand held steady since the last report. Expectations are for seasonal pickup in automobile sales over the summer, but aviation manufacturers expect sales to remain flat.

Agriculture Drought conditions improved slightly due to scattered rainfall in July. Crops remained mostly in fair to good shape, with the exception of dryland cotton crop in the Texas High Plains region which suffered due to lack of moisture. Overall, crop conditions were much better than a year ago. Drought in the Midwest has caused grain prices to climb sharply, squeezing margins for ranchers by driving up feed costs for livestock.

EX-99.1 d440140dex991.htm PRESS RELEASE Press Release Exhibit 99.1 For Immediate Release Media Relations Contact Randy Hargrove 800-331-0085 Investor Relations Contact Carol Schumacher 479-277-1498 Pre-recorded conference call 877-523-5612 (U.S. and Canada) 201-689-8483 (All other countries) Call passcode: 9256278 Walmart reports Q3 EPS of $1.08, reaffirms top end of full-year EPS guidance; Company is well positioned for Q4 holidays Q3 Highlights : Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. (Walmart) reported third quarter diluted earnings per share from continuing operations of $1.08, within guidance of $1.04 to $1.09. This was an 11.3 percent increase from the $0.97 per share reported for the third quarter last year.

Retail Sales Retail sales grew slightly over the reporting period and were up from a year ago. Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel. Sales growth in the Eleventh District remained stronger than the nation, on average, according to two large retailers. Retailers expect a seasonal pickup in demand in the fourth quarter, although sales will likely be down from last year. Automobile sales were mostly flat since the last report, but were up from year ago levels. Inventories were lighter than desired. Contacts said political uncertainty was hampering consumer confidence, and outlooks were cautious.

Prices Most responding firms said prices were unchanged from the last reporting period. However, accounting firms noted a modest rise in rates, airlines reported higher fares, and some construction-related manufacturers said they were able to raise selling prices as a result of improved demand. Overall, input costs were flat to down, with reports of lower prices for cotton, scrap metal, and steel. The recent decline in fuel prices lowered costs for airlines and freight transportation firms.

report.summary: Store 8 has 9 flagged departments, with $7,110 below the ML forecast (an ML estimate, not a verified loss). Walmart overall was close to forecast that week, and Horticulture and Swimwear fell at most stores in the region. The gaps in Furniture, Bras / Lingerie and Licensed Sports Apparel look local to this store, and no report or outside factor was found that explains them.

findings.title: Horticulture and Swimwear fell across many stores
findings.text: Most other stores also sold below the ML forecast in Dept 56 Horticulture and Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear that week. Store 8's drops are in line with that wider pattern, though Dept 56 (-42.9%) is a larger drop than the all-store median of -29.6%.

findings.title: Entertainment category drew a Walmart comment
findings.text: The Walmart Q2 earnings call on Aug 16, 2012 said "industry trends in electronics continue to impact the broader entertainment category." This is a general, company-wide comment, not a finding about Store 8. Dept 5 Media & Gaming also fell at most Texas stores.

findings.title: Some drops are larger than other stores
findings.text: Dept 71 Furniture (-28.4%), Dept 30 Bras / Lingerie (-28.6%) and Dept 41 Licensed Sports Apparel (-33.0%) fell much more here than the all-store medians, which were flat or up (+6.4%, -1.7% and +5.9%). This points to a store-specific cause rather than a shared one. Store 8's other departments were, overall, close to forecast (-0.4%).

findings.title: Outside factors show no clear shared cause
findings.text: No holiday was recorded that week. Local fuel prices were $3.42/gal vs $3.28 and temperatures were 85°F vs 81°F. Unemployment was 5.4% vs 5.4%. Walmart overall was at -0.4% of forecast, with 20 of 45 stores below it.

findings.title: Inventory and apparel comments in a later Fed report
findings.text: The Aug 29, 2012 Beige Book, which is dated after the week ending Aug 3, 2012, said "Inventories were lighter than desired" and noted "Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel." These are district-wide comments and do not name Store 8.

departments.what_supports_it: This is the largest percentage drop at Store 8 (-42.9%), and 27 of 34 other stores were also flagged. The Texas stores also fell (10 of 11 flagged), so this looks like a shared pattern, though the store's drop is deeper than the median.

This is the largest dollar gap ($3,217 below the ML forecast). The Walmart Q2 call mentions the entertainment category, and 11 of 13 Texas stores were below the ML forecast, but Store 8's -21.9% is well below the all-store median of -7.9%.
Drops were widespread: 35 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast, and 9 of 10 Texas stores were too. Store 8's -39.8% is close to the all-store median of -45.8%, so it fits the wider pattern.
The store's -28.6% is much larger than the all-store median of -1.7%, and the Aug 29 Beige Book notes apparel strength in the district, so no shared cause was found here.
The store's -28.4% is well below the all-store median of +6.4%, and no Texas store was flagged here. No report or outside factor was found for this department.
The store's -33.0% is far below the all-store median of +5.9%. Two other Texas stores were flagged, so there is some regional overlap, but no report or outside factor was found for it.

report.not_found: No Walmart-wide, regional or outside cause was found for the drops in Dept 71, Dept 30 or Dept 41 at Store 8; the reports reviewed do not mention those departments.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Comp sales in technology and entertainment, which continued to experience deflation, were slightly positive this quarter. Wireless, up double-digit comps, performed well and benefitted from both the Samsung Galaxy III and the Apple iPhone 5. Televisions and home theater comps are up low single-digit, driven by unit movement and improved availability in large screen televisions. Average selling prices continue to decrease for TVs, and our inventory position for the holidays is very good. Video games, music and movies continue to experience pressure in the current environment.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Most of our merchandising areas again delivered solid performance, though industry trends in electronics continue to impact the broader entertainment category. We're seeing market share growth across grocery and health & wellness. You can expect to hear more about market share and how we're using Nielsen data during our annual analyst meeting in October.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending increased moderately. Same-store sales at a Minnesota-based retailer increased 4 percent in August compared with a year ago. A Minneapolis area mall manger reported that sales over the past two months were up about 4 percent compared with a year earlier, while another Minneapolis mall reported that while traffic was flat, sales were up somewhat. In North Dakota, a mall manager reported that sales in August and September were up more than 5 percent from last year. Recent sales increased at a Minnesota-based women's apparel store. A domestic auto dealer reported strong sales activity near the end of September and solid commercial fleet sales. A representative of an auto dealers association in North Dakota reported strong vehicle sales across the state.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: The continued strong industry deflation led to a low single-digit negative comp for entertainment. Within wireless, a broader assortment resulted in double-digit comp sales growth, as customers continue to look at Walmart as a wireless destination. In media and gaming, we're well positioned for a very strong release schedule throughout the fourth quarter. Top releases like Halo and Call of Duty drove customers into our store over the last several weeks. Layaway drove a great deal of interest in toys, including toy construction, educational toys, ride-ons, and bicycles. We're well stocked in this season's must-have toys, and will be able to delight our younger customers all season long.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Our entertainment business had a low single-digit negative comp. While industry dynamics continued to pressure media and gaming, demand for tablets and tablet accessories remains strong. Customers continue to seek out the exclusive Walmart Straight Talk offering and our expanded assortment of smart phones. Straight Talk prepaid phones posted strong double-digit comp growth in the second quarter. We also introduced a solutions-focused merchandising approach that drove stronger printer and ink sales.

report.summary: Store 13 was below the ML forecast in five departments that week, and the largest gap was in Dept 58 Wireless Services. Outerwear and Store Supplies were also below the forecast at most other stores, which points to a wider pattern in those departments. The drop in Wireless and Optical looks more local to this store, and no report or outside factor explains it.

findings.title: Outerwear drop seen at most stores
findings.text: 31 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast in Dept 36 that week, with a median of -32.9%. This store's -50.1% sits within that wider pattern, so the cause may be broader than this store.

findings.title: Store Supplies below forecast everywhere
findings.text: All 14 other stores were below the ML forecast in Dept 99 that week, with a median of -81.0%. This store's -77.8% matches that pattern, which points to a shared cause across stores.

findings.title: Wireless drop is specific to this store
findings.text: Across all other stores, Dept 58 was +0.5% together, while this store was -33.1%, and the one other Rocky Mountain store was not flagged. This points to something local, such as stock, staffing or a local competitor, rather than a wider cause. The Nov 15, 2012 earnings call said "Wireless, up double-digit comps, performed well", which does not match this store's result.

findings.title: Optical is this store's largest gap
findings.text: 8 of 10 other stores were below the ML forecast in Dept 50 that week, but this store at -39.5% was the lowest of the 11 stores. The ML team's notes say the department was "model too high at most stores", and no Rocky Mountain store was flagged. The Aug 16, 2012 call said "We're seeing market share growth across grocery and health & wellness", which does not point to a category drop.

passages.text: Retail and Tourism First District retailers contacted for this round indicate that sales through mid to late September are slightly above 2011. Year-over-year sales increases in recent months range from low single-digit to high single-digit percentage gains, although one retailer reports that its 2012 sales to date are 2 percent to 3 percent below last year's. Furniture sales have picked up after declining during the summer, while spending on apparel and household items remains strong. Contacts express some concern that consumer sentiment could be negatively affected by domestic politics and the fiscal cliff, which increases their uncertainty about how well the end-of-year 2012 holiday sales season will turn out. While such concerns lead retailers to expect the U.S. economy will remain flat over the next 6 to 8 months, respondents are nonetheless cautiously optimistic that their 2012 revenues will end up slightly ahead of 2011 levels.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

Retail and Tourism First District retail contacts offer a very mixed take on economic conditions in the region. Demand remains strong for adult clothing, but spending on durable items such as furniture and electronics continues to be lower than earlier in the year. Some companies cite disappointing sales during the last six weeks, while others report some upside surprises. Sales results range from low single-digit declines to high single-digit increases compared with a year earlier. Some contacts say that consumer sentiment has become more negative, while others observe that consumers are "coming back." Retailers note wholesale prices remain flat so they are holding selling prices steady. Respondents still express uncertainty about the direction of the U.S. economy and say they expect little improvement over the next six to eight months.

Staffing Services New England staffing firms generally report lighter-than-expected volumes through mid-August, with most contacts characterizing business as "slow" or "flat." The May-to-August dip reportedly reflects a softening of demand for office and clerical assistants and light industrial workers. Nevertheless, year-over-year revenue changes in the second quarter remained largely positive, bolstered by steady demand from the engineering, legal, and IT sectors. The number of permanent and temporary-to-permanent placements continues to grow slowly, with one contact noting that clients are "definitely more willing to commit." Labor supply has gone largely unchanged since May.

The retail method requires management to make certain judgments and estimates that may significantly impact the ending inventory valuation at cost, as well as the amount of gross profit recognized. Judgments made include recording markdowns used to sell inventory and shrinkage. When management determines the salability of inventory has diminished, markdowns for clearance activity and the related cost impact are recorded. Factors considered in the determination of markdowns include current and anticipated demand, customer preferences and age of merchandise, as well as seasonal and fashion trends. Changes in weather patterns and customer preferences related to fashion trends could cause material changes in the amount and timing of markdowns from year to year.

passages.text: Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has firmed somewhat since the last report. Two major retail chains report that sales in the region were on plan in July and ahead of plan in early August. Similarly a major retail mall in upstate New York reports some firming in sales, as well as shopper traffic, in July and early August, following lackluster business in May and June. Retail prices continue to be described as steady--including apparel prices, which had previously been expected to drift down with the retreat in cotton prices earlier this year. Stores in New York City have performed on par or modestly better than those in the rest of the region. Inventories are generally said to be at or slightly above desired levels.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.text: In our consumables business where we continue to focus on price, we had solid increases in unit sales. Table-top and personal paper categories had mid single-digit increases. Our recent launch of the new Member's Mark paper plate is outselling comparable branded items and is creating additional margin that allows us to price more aggressively. Tobacco sales, which remain important for convenience store owners, were a drag on overall comp sales for the quarter, but that reduction helped drive a merchandising mix that was a positive to profit. Technology, entertainment and office achieved low single-digit comps. Performance was strong in portable electronics, including tablets, but challenged by continued softness in video games, movies, and books.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Now, the remainder of our discussion today is focused on our core business which excludes fuel for comparative purposes, unless otherwise noted.Net sales were $12.2 billion, up 3.6 percent from last year. Our strongest divisional performance was in the West, with our strongest regional performance in the Great Plains, Mid South, and Mid Atlantic. Now I'd like to turn your attention to merchandising. There were three major themes during the third quarter: price investment, moderation of inflation, and new product introduction.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Our apparel business posted a low single-digit comp increase, making this the third straight quarter of positive comps. The consistency of our apparel business and focus on basics, especially in kids, ladies, and men's, continues to drive growth, despite the impact of a warm October across much of the country. We have worked hard on improving item quality, focusing on the elements that our customers appreciate, and are optimistic that our current trend will continue into the holiday season.

Wages and Prices Price inflation remained quite limited for most final goods and services during the reporting period. Prices increased overall for some energy items including electricity, crude oil, and retail gasoline. Natural gas prices remained near historically low levels. Contacts noted high feed prices are passing through to grocery stores and restaurants. Contacts in the tech sector reported slightly lower prices of some technology-related products. For most products and services, vigorous competition among firms and cost-conscious purchasing behavior by consumers continued to keep price inflation in check.

Sam's Club is stepping up price investment for the holidays, and we are well prepared for our members' gifting and entertaining needs." Sam's Club expects comp sales, without fuel, for the current 13-week period ending Jan. 25, 2013, to increase between 1.5 percent and 3.5 percent. Last year, Sam's Club comp, without fuel, for the fourth quarter comparable 13-week period rose 5.4 percent. To align with the company's internal operating systems, Walmart will report comp sales for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2013 on a 4-5-4 basis and will not recognize a 53-week retail calendar this year. passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported modest increases in retail spending on a year-over-year basis, but many reported slower growth in recent months compared with earlier in the year; however, Boston and Cleveland reported sales as flat, and New York cited softer sales. There were a few reports that high summer temperatures negatively affected sales. Sales of big-ticket household goods were strong in the Richmond, Chicago, Kansas City, and Dallas Districts, while sales were reportedly flat for home furnishings and major appliances in the San Francisco District. Boston reported that sales for furniture and electronics had slowed, and retailers in the New York District reported that home goods sales were weak. Reports from luxury-goods retailers were mixed.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Most of our merchandising areas again delivered solid performance, though industry trends in electronics continue to impact the broader entertainment category. We're seeing market share growth across grocery and health & wellness. You can expect to hear more about market share and how we're using Nielsen data during our annual analyst meeting in October.

Consumer Spending Consumer spending improved with stronger than expected sales in June and was expected to strengthen further in the coming months. District retailers reported increased sales, particularly for seasonal items, mid-priced appliances, apparel, and fashion accessories. Several high-end retailers, however, commented that economic uncertainty had slowed demand for luxury items. Auto sales climbed sharply and were expected to remain solid for the next few months with more dealers offering sales incentives and discounts. Fuel-efficient cars sold well, while demand for large, expensive cars and trucks remained weak. Restaurant sales increased more than expected as both the number of diners and average check amounts edged up in June. Tourism activity ramped up with the start of the summer vacation season, though wildfires in Colorado hurt traffic in the Rocky Mountain region. District hotel owners reported a sharp rise in occupancy at higher average room rates and expected bookings to remain strong during the next three months.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Hello, this is Carol Schumacher, vice president of investor relations for Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. Thanks for joining us today for our earnings call to review the third quarter of fiscal 2013. All information for this quarter, including our unit counts, square footage, and financial metrics, is available on our website. New address: stock.walmart.com. Please note that while we update unit counts on a monthly basis on our website, in the earnings discussion today, units and square footage are referred to as of the quarter end. Our press release is available on the website, and a full transcript of this call has already been posted there. Here's the agenda for today's call.

Consumer Spending Consumer spending continued to increase in July and early August and was expected to rise further over the next three months. Retailers reported higher sales, though gains were a bit less than expected. Home furnishings, clothing and back-to-school items sold well, while sales of high-end jewelry were weaker. Auto sales increased sharply as more incentives were offered and access to credit improved slightly. Demand for small and mid-sized crossovers, SUVs and cars was strong, while demand for larger SUVs and minivans remained weak. Most auto dealers expected sales to strengthen further in the months ahead. Restaurant sales increased, and several contacts expected higher menu prices in coming months in response to rising food costs. After strong gains in June, hotel occupancy fell slightly in July and early August, but average room rates continued to rise. In terms of tourism, the number of visitors at local attractions grew slightly, and modest gains were expected in the months ahead.
