passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Our apparel business posted a low single-digit comp increase, making this the third straight quarter of positive comps. The consistency of our apparel business and focus on basics, especially in kids, ladies, and men's, continues to drive growth, despite the impact of a warm October across much of the country. We have worked hard on improving item quality, focusing on the elements that our customers appreciate, and are optimistic that our current trend will continue into the holiday season.

passages.section: Walmart U.S. Neighborhood Markets and Other Small Formats
passages.text: • Apparel includes apparel for women, girls, men, boys and infants, shoes, jewelry and accessories; and • Home includes home furnishings, housewares and small appliances, bedding, home décor, outdoor living and horticulture.

Net sales for the Walmart U.S. segment increased 3.6% and 4.4% for the three and nine months ended October 31, 2012, respectively, when compared to the same periods in the previous year. The increases in net sales were due to increases in comparable store sales of 1.5% and 2.5% as a result of improved ticket and traffic for the three and nine months ended October 31, 2012, respectively, combined with year-over-year growth in retail square feet of 2.1%. Walmart U.S.'s focus on expanded merchandise assortment and price leadership were key factors contributing to the sales performance. Gross profit rate declined 30 and 25 basis points for the three and nine months ended October 31, 2012, respectively, compared to the same periods in the previous year.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Now, the remainder of our discussion today is focused on our core business which excludes fuel for comparative purposes, unless otherwise noted.Net sales were $12.2 billion, up 3.6 percent from last year. Our strongest divisional performance was in the West, with our strongest regional performance in the Great Plains, Mid South, and Mid Atlantic. Now I'd like to turn your attention to merchandising. There were three major themes during the third quarter: price investment, moderation of inflation, and new product introduction.

Retail Trade and Services Retail sales rose further overall. Contacts reported sales were a bit stronger relative to the prior reporting period. Discount chains and online retailers continued to outperform traditional department stores. At grocery stores, consumer spending was soft as shoppers continued to shift their purchasing decisions in favor of cheaper products. Contacts reported a strong pace for auto sales, significantly above the pace from the same period last year. Demand for used vehicles also remained robust.

report.summary: Six departments at Store 28 sold below the ML forecast for the week ending Sep 21, 2012, a total of $4,530 (an ML estimate, not a verified loss). Apparel departments fell below forecast at many stores across the country, which points to a wider apparel pattern, though the drops at this store are larger than the typical store. Store 28's total sales were close to the forecast, so the drops are concentrated in a few departments.

findings.title: Apparel drops seen at many stores
findings.text: In Dept 33 Girlswear, 23 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast that week, and in Dept 31 Accessories, 36 of 42 were. Store 28 was also below forecast in both, so the drop is not limited to this store.

findings.title: Walmart-wide week close to forecast
findings.text: All 45 stores sold $44,210,995 against a $44,396,958 forecast (-0.4%), and 28 of 45 stores were below forecast. The overall week was close to forecast, so the Store 28 drops are not a company-wide shortfall.

findings.title: Store total near forecast, most departments below
findings.text: Store 28's total sales were $1,132,405 against a $1,146,785 forecast (-1.3%). But 49 of 69 departments were below forecast, so many smaller departments also fell short while the total stayed near the forecast.

findings.title: Weather and fuel changed little
findings.text: There was no holiday that week. Temperature was 83°F against 87°F in the prior 4-week median, and fuel was $4.12/gal against $4.11. Unemployment was unchanged at 10.9%. These changes are small, so they are unlikely to explain the whole gap alone.

findings.title: Report notes weather and soft grocery spending
findings.text: The Oct 10, 2012 Beige Book says "A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather." For the San Francisco district, it says "At grocery stores, consumer spending was soft." These are district-wide comments, not findings about Store 28.

findings.title: ML notes on forecast levels
findings.text: The ML team's notes list a signal that the forecast may be too high for Dept 56 Horticulture and Dept 99 Store Supplies. The notes also say the model was too high at most other stores in Dept 99. These are the ML team's own notes, not verified findings.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Wages and Prices Price inflation was limited for most final goods and services during the reporting period. Prices increased for some energy items, mainly crude oil, retail gasoline, and electricity, but natural gas prices remained near historic lows. Contacts also noted price increases for assorted food commodities, particularly grains, although meat prices reportedly have leveled off for the time being. For most products and services, vigorous competition among firms and cost-conscious purchasing behavior by consumers kept price inflation in check.

passages.text: Hello, this is Carol Schumacher, vice president of investor relations for Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. Thanks for joining us today for our earnings call to review the third quarter of fiscal 2013. All information for this quarter, including our unit counts, square footage, and financial metrics, is available on our website. New address: stock.walmart.com. Please note that while we update unit counts on a monthly basis on our website, in the earnings discussion today, units and square footage are referred to as of the quarter end. Our press release is available on the website, and a full transcript of this call has already been posted there. Here's the agenda for today's call.

report.summary: Lawn & Garden and Stamps / Service Plans were below the ML forecast at most stores that week, not just at Store 28, which points to a wider cause that is possible but not verified. Seafood and Horticulture show a mixed picture across stores, and Cosmetics was not down elsewhere. No holiday or report passage names these departments, so the explanation for the store's gaps remains open.

findings.title: Lawn & Garden down at most stores
findings.text: 39 of 44 other stores were also below the ML forecast in Lawn & Garden that week, with a median of -13.2% and all together at -11.0%. Store 28 was at -25.9%, which is in line with the wider pattern rather than unusual for the chain. The ML team's notes list the recent and seasonal declines as signals.

findings.title: West Coast stores mostly below forecast
findings.text: In the West Coast region, 5 of 5 other stores were below the ML forecast in Lawn & Garden, and 4 of 5 were below in Stamps / Service Plans and in Seafood. Only Cosmetics stayed mostly above forecast in the region. A regional pattern like this suggests a shared cause, but none has been confirmed.

findings.title: Walmart overall was not down
findings.text: Across all 45 stores that week, sales were $47,338,695 against a $46,950,212 forecast, which is +0.8%. Store 28 as a whole was -4.0% below its forecast, with 51 of 68 departments below, so the store's gap is broader than its five flagged departments.

findings.title: Outside factors show little clear link
findings.text: There was no holiday that week. Local fuel was $4.00/gal against $3.76 in the prior weeks and temperature was 95°F against 91°F, while unemployment was unchanged at 10.9%. These changes are possible contributors, but no source ties them to these departments. Store-level markdowns of $14,525 are recorded for the whole store and cannot be tied to any department.

findings.title: Report gives only general context
findings.text: The Federal Reserve Beige Book of Aug 29, 2012 reported that "retail spending in July and early August was up" nationally. It noted that San Francisco saw "strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June". It does not mention Lawn & Garden, Seafood, Stamps / Service Plans, Horticulture or Cosmetics, and it describes regions as a whole, not this store.

departments.what_supports_it: The largest dollar gap at $1,874 (-25.9%), and 39 of 44 other stores were also below the ML forecast that week, which suggests a category-wide pattern. The ML notes show the same season in earlier years was -25.1%.

32 of 44 other stores were below the ML forecast and 20 were also flagged, with 3 of 5 regional stores flagged, so this is a broad pattern. The ML notes show this week at -26.3% against the recent 4-week median and -40.8% against the same season in earlier years.

22 of 41 other stores were below the ML forecast, a mixed result with a median of -0.6%, so the pattern is weaker than Lawn & Garden. The ML notes show this week at -16.6% against the recent 4-week median, but +23.4% against the same season in earlier years.

21 of 38 other stores were below the ML forecast, but all stores together were +2.0%, so the drop looks specific to this store and region. The ML notes show this week at -37.1% against the recent 4-week median and -60.4% against the same season in earlier years.

Cosmetics is the weakest case: 14 of 33 other stores were below forecast, but all stores together were +6.2% and none of the 3 regional stores were below forecast. No store-side or wider evidence was found for the -26.1% gap.

report.not_found: I looked for holiday effects, report passages naming these departments, and store-level explanations, and found none beyond general economic context.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has firmed somewhat since the last report. Two major retail chains report that sales in the region were on plan in July and ahead of plan in early August. Similarly a major retail mall in upstate New York reports some firming in sales, as well as shopper traffic, in July and early August, following lackluster business in May and June. Retail prices continue to be described as steady--including apparel prices, which had previously been expected to drift down with the retreat in cotton prices earlier this year. Stores in New York City have performed on par or modestly better than those in the rest of the region. Inventories are generally said to be at or slightly above desired levels.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

report.summary: Store 24's drop in these seven departments is part of a wider dip. Walmart overall was below the ML forecast that week, and most of the store's other departments were also below it. The regional reports describe steady or firming sales rather than a clear drop, and no report names these departments, so the specific cause remains unexplained.

findings.title: Walmart-wide dip that week
findings.text: Across all 45 stores, sales were $47,131,887 against a $48,409,634 ML forecast (-2.6%), and 35 of 45 stores were below the forecast. Store 24 was $1,343,995 against $1,414,320 (-5.0%), so it fell further than the chain as a whole.

findings.title: Store-wide dip across many departments
findings.text: 55 of Store 24's 71 departments were below the ML forecast that week, not only the 7 flagged ones. The dip was spread across most of the store, which points to a store-wide factor rather than one department.

findings.title: Same departments down at other stores
findings.text: Store Supplies was below the ML forecast at all 14 other stores, with a median of -77.6%. Plus & Maternity (26 of 36 other stores below, median -13.7%) and Fabrics & Crafts (23 of 26 below, median -17.3%) also fell at many stores, though Store 24's drops were deeper than most.

findings.title: Regional and report context mostly positive
findings.text: The New York Fed's Beige Book said retail sales firmed in July and early August, and reported that "Two major retail chains report that sales in the region were on plan in July and ahead of plan in early August." The same report said "Inventories are generally said to be at or slightly above desired levels," so stock shortages are not indicated at district level. Store 24's other New York State peers were mostly not flagged, so the drop looks deeper here than in the region.

findings.title: Holiday, fuel and weather changes were small
findings.text: No holiday fell in the week ending Aug 31, 2012. Local fuel was $4.03/gal against $3.91, temperature 71°F against 73°F, and unemployment 9.0% in both periods. These changes are small, and the evidence does not link them to the specific departments.

findings.title: Wireless Services drop and Walmart phone context
findings.text: Wireless Services was $1,595 against $2,525 (-36.8%), and the one other New York State store in that department was also flagged. Walmart's second-quarter report said "Straight Talk prepaid phones posted strong double-digit comp growth in the second quarter," which does not clearly match a broad decline in this category.

13 of 22 other stores were below the ML forecast (median -7.8%), and the one other New York State store was flagged. Walmart's second-quarter report describes strong prepaid phone growth, which does not clearly explain a decline here.
8 of 10 other stores were below the ML forecast (median -16.0%), so the drop is partly shared. Two of those stores were also flagged, and Store 24 at -37.6% is deeper than most.
26 of 40 other stores were below the ML forecast, but the median was only -5.9%, so this is a mild shared dip. Store 24's -28.7% is deeper than typical.
23 of 26 other stores were below the ML forecast (median -17.3%), and both New York State peers were below. Store 24's -36.9% is the deepest in its group, so a local factor is possible.
